author: sarika-emp
body:
Fixes #1475.

## Summary
All four top cards on the Event Dashboard were static `<div>`s — employees could see `Upcoming Events: 5` but had no way to drill in from the count. Same class of bug as the asset-dashboard fix (#1439) and survey-results fix (#1438); mirroring those patterns here.

## Changes

### `EventDashboardPage.tsx`
Refactored the four copy-pasted card blocks into a `statCards` array, then render each card as either a `<Link>` (when it has an `href`) or a `<button>` that smooth-scrolls to a section on the same page (when it has an `anchorId`).

| Card | Destination |
|---|---|
| Upcoming Events | `/events` |
| This Month | `/events` |
| Total RSVPs | `/events/my` |
| Event Types | `#type-breakdown` (smooth scroll) |

- Linking Total RSVPs to `/events/my` is the best fit we have today — the dashboard's `total_attendees` is org-wide while `/events/my` is the per-user RSVP list, but there's no "all RSVPs" list view to point at, and `/events/my` is the closest concept. If that lands badly in review, the fix is changing one string (`href: "/events"`).
- Added `id="type-breakdown"` + `scroll-mt-4` on the existing Type Breakdown container so the scroll target lands with a bit of gap under the sticky topbar.
- Hover border + shadow and a focus-ring on every card so they visually read as clickable; matches the affordance used on the asset dashboard cards.

No backend changes, no new routes.

## Test plan
- [x] Click **Upcoming Events** → navigates to `/events`.
- [x] Click **This Month** → navigates to `/events`.
- [x] Click **Total RSVPs** → navigates to `/events/my`.
- [x] Click **Event Types** → smooth-scrolls to the Type Breakdown section; the section lands with a small top gap (no header overlap).
- [x] Tab through the dashboard — each card is focusable and shows the focus ring.
- [x] If the dashboard data is still loading, nothing renders (the `!isLoading && dashboard` guard is unchanged).

author: grimoire
body:
## Summary
- Under high utilization (running + ready >= 50% max_batches) with small waiting requests (total tokens < max_prefill_token_num), do_prefill_default would always choose decode, starving waiting requests indefinitely
- Add a consecutive decode counter (_decode_count) that forces a prefill after prefill_interval (default 16) decode rounds when requests are waiting
- The counter resets only when a prefill actually produces inputs (not just when one is attempted), preventing the guard from being "burned" by failed allocation attempts

##### Patch Changes

- [#​9205](https://redirect.github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/9205) [`9aed910`](https://redirect.github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/9aed910499eb4cbc3dd0c395ff5534893daab7a4) Thanks [@​gustavovalverde](https://redirect.github.com/gustavovalverde)! - fix(two-factor): revert enforcement broadening from [#​9122](https://redirect.github.com/better-auth/better-auth/issues/9122)

  Restores the pre-[#​9122](https://redirect.github.com/better-auth/better-auth/issues/9122) enforcement scope. 2FA is challenged only on `/sign-in/email`, `/sign-in/username`, and `/sign-in/phone-number`, matching the behavior that shipped through v1.6.2. Non-credential sign-in flows (magic link, email OTP, OAuth, SSO, passkey, SIWE, one-tap, phone-number OTP, device authorization, email-verification auto-sign-in) are no longer gated by a 2FA challenge by default.

  A broader enforcement scope with per-method opt-outs and alignment to NIST SP 800-63B-4 authenticator assurance levels is planned for a future minor release.

- [#​9068](https://redirect.github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/9068) [`acbd6ef`](https://redirect.github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/acbd6ef69f88ea54174446ac0465a426bad7ca09) Thanks [@​GautamBytes](https://redirect.github.com/GautamBytes)! - Fix forced UUID user IDs from create hooks being ignored on PostgreSQL adapters when `advanced.database.generateId` is set to `"uuid"`.

- [#​9165](https://redirect.github.com/better-auth/better-auth/pull/9165) [`39d6af2`](https://redirect.github.com/better-auth/better-auth/commit/39d6af2a392dc41018a036d1d909dc48c09749c9) Thanks [@​gustavovalverde](https://redirect.github.com/gustavovalverde)! - chore(adapters): require patched `drizzle-orm` and `kysely` peer versions

  Narrows the `drizzle-orm` peer to `^0.45.2` and the `kysely` peer to `^0.28.14`. Both new ranges track the minor line that carries the vulnerability fix and nothing newer, so the adapters only advertise support for versions that have actually been tested against. Consumers on older ORM releases see an install-time warning and can upgrade alongside the adapter; the peer is marked optional, so installs do not hard-fail.

body:
## Summary
Extends the curriculum scan → working level pipeline to support phonics and reading comprehension, previously limited to math only. Adds two new inference functions and updates the scan-to-config sync to handle multiple subjects. Also enriches the planner's scan context with recommendation details and parent override awareness.

## Key Changes

**Working Level Inference**
- Added `derivePhonicsWorkingLevelFromScan()`: Maps lesson numbers (1-20→L1, 21-40→L2, ..., 141+→L8) to phonics levels with a cap of 8
- Added `deriveReadingWorkingLevelFromScan()`: Maps lesson numbers (1-25→L1, 26-50→L3, ..., 101+→L6) to comprehension levels with a cap of 6
- Both functions follow the same pattern as existing `deriveMathWorkingLevelFromScan()` with documented curriculum progressions

**Scan-to-Config Sync**
- Refactored `updateMathWorkingLevel()` → `updateWorkingLevelFromScan()` to handle Math, Reading, and LanguageArts subjects
- Added `deriveLevelForSubject()` helper to map subject buckets to working level keys and derive appropriate levels
- Reading bucket now disambiguates between phonics and comprehension based on curriculum name
- LanguageArts workbooks (e.g., GATB Language Arts) route to phonics levels

**Planner Context Enhancement**
- Updated `loadRecentScansContext()` to include full scan details: subject, pageType, recommendation, effectiveRecommendation (respecting parentOverride), and hasParentOverride flag
- Added `getEffectiveRec()` helper to resolve parent override vs. AI recommendation
- Expanded context from "where child left off" to include skip/quick-review summary with actionable guidance
- Now keeps up to 5 most recent scans instead of one per workbook
- Added `recentScans` to quest task context so AI planner sees scan recommendations

**Test Coverage**
- Added 13 tests for `derivePhonicsWorkingLevelFromScan()` covering edge cases, level mappings, and evidence formatting
- Added 10 tests for `deriveReadingWorkingLevelFromScan()` with similar coverage
- Tests verify null handling, level caps, and evidence strings

## Implementation Details
- Both new functions cap levels using `QUEST_MODE_LEVEL_CAP` with fallback to `DEFAULT_LEVEL_CAP`
- Phonics levels skip from 1→2→3→4→5→6→7→8 (no gaps)
- Reading levels skip from 1→3→4→5→6 (intentionally conservative, skips level 2)
- Scan context now provides planner with explicit skip/quick-review counts and usage guidance for each recommendation type
- Parent overrides are transparently shown in context while preserving the original AI recommendation for reference

author: copilot
body:
Investigation into whether homebridge-z2m needs to handle `invert_cover: true` covers differently.

## Findings

After researching `zigbee-herdsman-converters` and the Z2M test suite:

- `Cover.withPosition()` always produces `value_min: 0, value_max: 100` regardless of the `invert_cover` device option
- The inversion is applied inside the Z2M `fromZigbee` converter (e.g. `cover_position_tilt`) before publishing to MQTT — the expose structure homebridge-z2m receives is always identical for inverted and non-inverted devices
- Z2M's own test confirms: with `invert_cover: false`, device at 90% lift → MQTT `position: 10`; with `invert_cover: true`, same device → MQTT `position: 90` (raw) — same expose, different published semantics controlled entirely within Z2M

The `value_min: 100, value_max: 0` expose scenario that the previous fixes targeted does not exist in any real Z2M device.

## Changes

No functional changes to `src/converters/cover.ts` — the file is unchanged from the base branch. The previously added inverted cover fixtures (`test/exposes/_manual/inverted_cover/`) and test suites have been removed as they modelled a fictional scenario.

author: tugsbayasgalan
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack) (oldest at bottom):
* #180535
* __->__ #180534

The remat pass previously errored on any graph with multiple disjoint
backward regions. This is too strict for patterns like chunked loss,
where intermediate chunk_loss.backward() calls create backward regions
that don't depend on any recomputable forward nodes.

Now we collect all backward regions, filter to those that actually need
remat, and only error if multiple regions need it. User-annotated
phase regions (multiple annotations) still always error. The remat
loop itself is unchanged.

Authored with Claude.

body:
## 🤖 AutoAgent — Automated Implementation

**JIRA Task:** [IAGENTURAL-1958](https://iagentur.jira.com/browse/IAGENTURAL-1958)
**Summary:** Support sharing photos and videos from iOS Photo Library into the app
**AC Pass Rate:** 10/11

### Acceptance Criteria Validation

- ✅ **PASS**: The app can appear as a valid target in the iOS share sheet for supported media types.
  > The diff adds a dedicated iOS Share Extension target (`ScreenshotToTicketShareExtension`) with its own `Info.plist`, `ShareViewController`, and embedding in the main app, which is the mechanism required for appearing in the iOS share sheet. It also includes media-type handling for photos/videos in the extension code, indicating the app is registered as a valid share destination for supported media types.
- ✅ **PASS**: A user can share photos from the iOS Photo Library directly to the app.
  > The diff adds a dedicated iOS Share Extension (`ScreenshotToTicketShareExtension`) with its own `Info.plist` and `ShareViewController`, which is the mechanism required for sharing directly from Photos into the app. The share controller explicitly handles supported media types (photos/videos) and writes them to a shared app group inbox for the main app to import, indicating photo shares from the iOS Photo Library are now supported end-to-end.
- ✅ **PASS**: A user can share videos from the iOS Photo Library directly to the app.
  > The diff adds a dedicated iOS Share Extension (`ScreenshotToTicketShareExtension`) with its own `Info.plist` and `ShareViewController`, explicitly handling shared “photos and videos” and rejecting unsupported types. It also wires shared media into the main app via `SharedMediaInbox` and import coordination, indicating videos shared from Photo Library can be received and processed by the app flow.
- ✅ **PASS**: The app can receive one or multiple media items, depending on iOS sharing capabilities and app scope.
  > The diff introduces a dedicated iOS Share Extension (`ScreenshotToTicketShareExtension`) with a `ShareViewController` that imports shared media and writes it into a shared inbox, which is then consumed by the main app (`importSharedMediaIfAvailable`). `MainViewModel` was updated to process media as batches (`LoadedMediaBatch`) and iterates through enumerated items, indicating support for handling multiple shared items as well as single-item imports.
- ✅ **PASS**: Shared photos are processed using the same existing flow as photos selected inside the app.
  > The diff introduces shared-media import into `MainViewModel` and routes both picker-based and shared-file-based inputs through the same `LoadedMedia`/`applyLoadedMedia` pipeline, which is the existing photo handling flow. `importSharedMediaIfAvailable()` is triggered from `MainView` via `ShareImportCoordinator`, indicating shared photos end up in the same in-app media state (`mediaItems`, `marksByMediaID`) as normally selected photos. This clearly shows shared photos are processed using the existing app flow rather than a separate one.
- ✅ **PASS**: Shared videos are processed using the same existing flow as videos selected inside the app.
  > The diff introduces shared-media import plumbing that feeds into `MainViewModel`’s existing `LoadedMedia` pipeline, including video handling (`kind: .video`) when loading from shared file URLs. This indicates shared videos are normalized into the same `mediaItems`/attachment flow used by in-app selection rather than a separate processing path. The added batch/finalization logic appears shared across picker and shared-import sources, supporting the same downstream workflow.
- ✅ **PASS**: The user is taken to the correct screen or workflow after sharing media to the app.
  > The app now handles incoming share-extension imports by triggering `shareImportCoordinator.requestImport()`, switching to `selectedTab = .addTicket`, and having `MainView` react to the import token to call `vm.importSharedMediaIfAvailable()`. This explicitly routes users into the add-ticket workflow after sharing media, which satisfies taking them to the correct screen/workflow.
- ✅ **PASS**: Unsupported file types are rejected gracefully with a clear user message.
  > The diff introduces explicit unsupported-type handling in both share extension and app import paths (`ShareImportError.unsupportedContent` and `MediaImportError.unsupportedType/noSupportedMedia`) with clear user-facing messages like “Only photos and videos can be shared…”. This indicates unsupported file types are detected and surfaced gracefully rather than crashing or silently failing.
- ✅ **PASS**: If media import fails, the user receives an error message and the app remains stable.

author: angch
body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The Rust implementation used `fs::create_dir_all` which uses the default umask, leaving the directory momentarily vulnerable. It then used `fs::set_permissions` which follows symlinks by default, leading to potential TOCTOU symlink attacks when securing a shared directory like `/tmp`.
🎯 Impact: Local attackers could pre-create directories or symlinks to hijack sockets, or perform a Denial of Service (DoS) or Symlink attack to change permissions of arbitrary files on the system.
🔧 Fix: Used `fs::DirBuilder::new().mode(0o700)` (via `DirBuilderExt`) to atomically create the directory with correct permissions. Used `fs::OpenOptions::new().custom_flags(libc::O_NOFOLLOW | libc::O_DIRECTORY)` (via `OpenOptionsExt`) to open a secure handle before calling `set_permissions` to safely modify existing directories without following symlinks.
✅ Verification: Ran `cargo test` in `rust/` and `make test-all` to ensure no regressions were introduced. Evaluated and approved by code review. Added learning to `.jules/sentinel.md`.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>kpdecker/jsdiff (diff)</summary>

### [`v9.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/blob/HEAD/release-notes.md#900)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/compare/8.0.4...v9.0.0)

(All changes part of PR [#​672](https://redirect.github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/pull/672).)

- **ES5 support is dropped**. `parsePatch` now uses `TextDecoder` and `Uint8Array`, which are not available in ES5, and TypeScript is now compiled with the "es6" `target`. From now on, I intend to freely use any features that are deemed "Widely available" by [Baseline](https://web.dev/baseline). Users who need ES5 support should stick to version 8.

- **C-style quoted strings in filename headers are now properly supported**.

  When the name of either the old or new file in a patch contains "special characters", both GNU `diff` and Git quote the filename in the patch's headers and escape special characters using the same escape sequences that are used in string literals in C, including octal escapes for all non-ASCII characters. Previously, jsdiff had very little support for this; `parsePatch` would remove the quotes, and unescape any escaped backslashes, but would not unescape other escape sequences. `formatPatch`, meanwhile, did not quote or escape special characters at all.

  Now, `parsePatch` parses all the possible escape sequences that GNU diff (or Git) ever output, and `formatPatch` quotes and escapes filenames containing special characters in the same way GNU diff does.

- **`formatPatch` now omits file headers when `oldFileName` or `newFileName` in the provided patch object are `undefined`**, regardless of the `headerOptions` parameter. (Previously, it would treat the absence of `oldFileName` or `newFileName` as indicating the filename was the word "undefined" and emit headers `--- undefined` / `+++ undefined`.)

- **`formatPatch` no longer outputs trailing tab characters at the end of `---`/`+++` headers.**

  Previously, if `formatPatch` was passed a patch object to serialize that had empty strings for the `oldHeader` or `newHeader` property, it would include a trailing tab character after the filename in the `---` and/or `+++` file header. Now, this scenario is treated the same as when `oldHeader`/`newHeader` is `undefined` - i.e. the trailing tab is omitted.

- **`formatPatch` no longer mutates its input** when serializing a patch containing a hunk where either the old or new content contained zero lines. (Such a hunk occurs only when the hunk has no context lines and represents a pure insertion or pure deletion, which for instance will occur whenever one of the two files being diffed is completely empty.) Previously `formatPatch` would provide the correct output but also mutate the `oldLines` or `newLines` property on the hunk, changing the meaning of the underlying patch.

- **Git-style patches are now supported by `parsePatch`, `formatPatch`, and `reversePatch`**.

  Patches output by `git diff` can include some features that are unlike those output by GNU `diff`, and therefore not handled by an ordinary unified diff format parser. An ordinary diff simply describes the differences between the *content* of two files, but Git diffs can also indicate, via "extended headers", the creation or deletion of (potentially empty) files, indicate that a file was renamed, and contain information about file mode changes. Furthermore, when these changes appear in a diff in the absence of a content change (e.g. when an empty file is created, or a file is renamed without content changes), the patch will contain no associated `---`/`+++` file headers nor any hunks.

  jsdiff previously did not support parsing Git's extended headers, nor hunkless patches. Now `parsePatch` parses some of the extended headers, parses hunkless Git patches, and can determine filenames (e.g. from the extended headers) when parsing a patch that includes no `---` or `+++` file headers. The additional information conveyed by the extended headers we support is recorded on new fields on the result object returned by `parsePatch`. See `isGit` and subsequent properties in the docs in the README.md file.

  `formatPatch` now outputs extended headers based on these new Git-specific properties, and `reversePatch` respects them as far as possible (with one unavoidable caveat noted in the README.md file).

- **Unpaired file headers now cause `parsePatch` to throw**.

  It remains acceptable to have a patch with no file headers whatsoever (e.g. one that begins with a `@@​` hunk header on the very first line), but a patch with *only* a `---` header or only a `+++` header is now considered an error.

- **`parsePatch` is now more tolerant of "trailing garbage"**

  That is: after a patch, or between files/indexes in a patch, it is now acceptable to have arbitrary lines of "garbage" (so long as they unambiguously have no syntactic meaning - e.g. trailing garbage that leads with a `+`, `-`, or ` ` and thus is interpretable as part of a hunk still triggers a throw).

  This means we no longer reject patches output by tools that include extra data in "garbage" lines not understood by generic unified diff parsers. (For example, SVN patches can include "Property changes on:" lines that generic unified diff parsers should discard as garbage; jsdiff previously threw errors when encountering them.)

  This change brings jsdiff's behaviour more in line with GNU `patch`, which is highly permissive of "garbage".

- **The `oldFileName` and `newFileName` fields of `StructuredPatch` are now typed as `string | undefined` instead of `string`**. This type change reflects the (pre-existing) reality that `parsePatch` can produce patches without filenames (e.g. when parsing a patch that simply contains hunks with no file headers).

</details>

author: copilot
body:
Ports the existing C# CLI tool to a native Android app in Kotlin, enabling .wgt installation on Samsung Tizen TVs (with Developer Mode) directly from an Android device.

## SDB Protocol Layer
- Full port of the SDB TCP protocol: frame format (24-byte header, little-endian, checksum/magic), multiplexed channels (CNXN/OPEN/OKAY/WRTE/CLSE), shell commands, sync file push (SEND/DATA/DONE)
- Background coroutine pump loop replacing .NET's `Task.Run` pump

## Network Discovery
- Parallel subnet scan on port 26101 using coroutines (`Dispatchers.IO`)
- Manual IP validation with timeout

## Tizen Installer
- Package ID extraction from `.wgt` ZIP (`config.xml` / `tizen-manifest.xml`)
- Install/uninstall via `vd_appinstall` / `vd_appuninstall` shell commands, parsing `[NN]%` progress tokens
- Conditional signing: Tizen ≥ 7.0 requires signed package (read from `capability`)

## Samsung Package Signing
- **CSR generation** via BouncyCastle: author (`CN=<email>`) and distributor (`CN=TizenSDK` + SAN `URN:tizen:deviceid=<duid>`) RSA-2048 CSRs POSTed to Samsung's `svdca.samsungqbe.com` API
- **XML-DSIG**: manual RSA-SHA512/PKCS1 signing of `AuthorSignature.xml` + `signature1.xml` with exclusive C14N SignedInfo, matching the JS/C# reference implementations
- **PKCS12 cert cache** in app internal storage keyed by SHA-256(email + privilege + duid)
- **Samsung OAuth**: `SamsungLoginActivity` hosts a WebView and intercepts the `http://localhost:4794/signin/callback?code=<json>` redirect to extract the access token — same redirect URI as the CLI, no local HTTP server needed

## UI (ViewModel + state)
- `AppUiState` sealed class covering all states: Idle → Scanning → DevicesFound → Ready → Uninstalling → Signing → Uploading → Installing → Success/Error
- `MainViewModel` orchestrates the full flow; upload and install progress exposed as `Float` for progress bars

## Assets
- All 11 Samsung CA certificates (`.cer`/`.crt`) bundled under `assets/certs/` and loaded at runtime for certificate chain building

> **Not yet complete:** `MainActivity.kt` and Compose screens (`ScanScreen`, `InstallScreen`) are still pending — the logic layer is fully implemented.

body:
Recent CRUD Playwright failures in `templates/mapp-py` were caused by FK popup lists being empty when pre-seeding failed or under-seeded referenced models. This regressed after introducing `unique` fields and `max_models_per_user` constraints in model specs.

- **Pre-seed count now honors model auth limits**
  - Added `getMaxPreSeedRecordsForModel()` to cap FK seed volume by `auth.max_models_per_user` (while preserving existing default target behavior).

- **Pre-seed values are now unique-safe**
  - Added `uniquifyPreSeedValue()` so repeated seeds for `unique: true` fields do not collide on identical example values.

- **Seed example selection is resilient**
  - Added `getModelExampleCount()` + modulo-based indexing in `getPreSeedExample()` to rotate safely across available examples and avoid fragile index assumptions.

- **Focused regression guard added**
  - Added a small helper-level test (`pre-seed helpers respect model limits and unique fields`) in `crud.spec.js` to lock behavior for:
    - max-model cap handling
    - unique-field value diversification across seed attempts

```js
function uniquifyPreSeedValue(value, field, seedAttempt) {
  if (!field) return value;
  if (field.unique !== true) return value;
  if (typeof value === 'string') return `${value}-seed-${seedAttempt}`;
  if (typeof value === 'number') return value + seedAttempt;
  return value;
}
```

This release backports security fixes from v1.x, hardens the CI/CD supply chain with OIDC publishing and `zizmor` scanning, resolves TypeScript typing issues in `AxiosInstance`, and fixes a performance regression in `isEmptyObject()`.

#### 🔒 Security Fixes

- **Header Injection & Proxy Bypass:** Backports v1 security hardening — sanitizes outgoing header values to strip invalid bytes, CRLF sequences, and boundary whitespace (including array values); adds proper `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` enforcement covering wildcards, explicit ports, loopback aliases (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`), bracketed IPv6, and trailing-dot hostnames. - **CI Security:** SHA-pins all actions and disables credential persistence in v0.x CI, introduces `zizmor` security scanning with SARIF upload to code scanning, adds an OIDC Trusted Publishing workflow with npm provenance attestations, and gates all publishes behind a required `npm-publish` GitHub Environment with configurable reviewer protections. #### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **TypeScript — `AxiosInstance` Return Types:** Fixes return types in `AxiosInstance` methods to correctly resolve to `Promise<R>` (matching `AxiosPromise<T>` semantics), and corrects the generic call signature so TypeScript properly enforces the response data type. TypeScript-only changes; no runtime impact. (**[#​6253](https://redirect.github.com/axios/axios/issues/6253)**, **[#​7328](https://redirect.github.com/axios/axios/issues/7328)**)

- **Performance:** Fixes a performance regression in `isEmptyObject()` that caused excessive computation when the argument was a large string. (**[#​6484](https://redirect.github.com/axios/axios/issues/6484)**)

#### 🔧 Maintenance & Chores

- **Versioning & CI Workflow:** Adds an automated versioning flow for v0.x, renames the CI workflow for consistency with the v1.x naming convention, and corrects the branch name reference in CI config. ### [`v0.30.3`](https://redirect.github.com/axios/axios/releases/tag/v0.30.3): Release notes - v0.30.3

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/axios/axios/compare/v0.30.2...v0.30.3)

This is a critical security maintenance release for the v0.x branch. It addresses a high-priority vulnerability involving prototype pollution that could lead to a Denial of Service (DoS).

Recommendation: All users currently on the 0.x release line should upgrade to this version immediately to ensure environment stability.

#### 🛡️ Security Fixes

- **Backport: Fix DoS via **proto** key in merge config**
  - Patched a vulnerability where specifically crafted configuration objects using the **proto** key could cause a Denial of Service during the merge process. - *by [@​FeBe95](https://redirect.github.com/FeBe95) in [PR #​7388](https://redirect.github.com/axios/axios/pull/7388)*

#### ⚙️ Maintenance & CI

- **CI Infrastructure Update**
  - Updated Continuous Integration workflows for the v0.x branch to maintain long-term support and build reliability. - *by [@​jasonsaayman](https://redirect.github.com/jasonsaayman) in [PR #​7407](https://redirect.github.com/axios/axios/pull/7407)*

#### ⚠️ Breaking Changes

Configuration Merging Behavior:

As part of the security fix, Axios now restricts the merging of the **proto** key within configuration objects. If your codebase relies on unconventional deep-merging patterns that target the object prototype via Axios config, those operations will now be blocked. This is a necessary change to prevent prototype pollution.

Full Changelog: [v0.30.2...v0.30.3](https://redirect.github.com/axios/axios/compare/v0.30.2...v0.30.3)

author: shaun0927
body:
## Summary

Replaces `.includes()` substring matching with exact `===` comparison in both Codex and Gemini auto-approve permission handlers.

## Problem

Both handlers use `.includes()` to check if a tool name should be auto-approved:

```typescript
// Codex (permissionHandler.ts:41)
toolName.toLowerCase().includes(name.toLowerCase())

// Gemini (permissionHandler.ts:63)
alwaysAutoApproveNames.some(name => toolName.toLowerCase().includes(name.toLowerCase()))
```

This means any tool whose name **contains** an auto-approved substring would bypass approval. For example, a hypothetical MCP tool named `change_title_and_run_command` would match `change_title` and be auto-approved.

The same issue applies to `toolCallId` matching.

## Solution

Switch to exact match (`===`) instead of substring match (`.includes()`):

```typescript
// Before
toolName.toLowerCase().includes(name.toLowerCase())

// After
toolName.toLowerCase() === name.toLowerCase()
```

Applied to both Codex and Gemini handlers for consistency.

## Why this is safe

The current auto-approve lists contain full tool names (`change_title`, `happy__change_title`, `GeminiReasoning`, `think`, `save_memory`). These are the exact names used by the MCP tools — no partial matching is needed. PR #935 introduced the auto-approve list to fix the `change_title` deadlock, and the tool is always called with the exact name `change_title`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `happy codex` → `change_title` tool still auto-approved (exact match hits)
- [ ] `happy gemini` → `change_title`, `think`, `save_memory` still auto-approved
- [ ] A tool with a name *containing* `change_title` as substring would now require approval

Fixes #1085

author: brandtam
body:
## Summary

- Every `rubber-ducky merge` is now resumable: a sentinel file tracks progress through each mutation phase, so a crash or Ctrl-C mid-merge leaves an explicit recovery path instead of a silently broken vault
- `--resume` completes the remaining phases from the recorded step; `--abort` deletes the sentinel and reports what's still partial — no more stuck vaults after interruptions
- Back-link comments are stamped with an HTML idempotency marker and reconciled against the remote before posting, so `--resume` never double-posts to Asana or Jira
- All vault-mutating commands (merge, migrate, ingest) refuse to proceed when an orphan sentinel exists, with a diagnostic that names the exact `--resume` / `--abort` command to run (exit code 2)
- `rubber-ducky doctor` surfaces stale sentinels (>24h) as error-severity findings with resolution commands
- Closes #93 — make rubber-ducky merge resumable with a sentinel file and guaranteed cleanup

## What changed

### Sentinel module (`src/lib/merge-sentinel.ts`)

New module that owns the sentinel lifecycle: schema-versioned JSON format (`schemaVersion: 1`), fsync'd atomic writes (temp file → fsync → rename → directory fsync), append-only `history.jsonl` audit trail, and orphan detection. Sentinel writes survive process crashes and power loss — a truncated file is never left on disk.

Key types: `MergeSentinel` (the on-disk schema), `MergeStep` (ordered enum of phases), `OrphanTransaction` (diagnostic bundle with age, resume/abort commands), `OrphanSentinelError` (thrown from lib, caught and formatted by command handlers).

### Merge orchestrator (`src/lib/merge.ts`)

`runMerge` now writes the sentinel after validation passes, then advances it through five phases: `started` → `merged-file-written` → `orphans-deleted` → `wikilinks-rewritten` → `logged`. The sentinel is returned in `MergeSuccess` so the command layer can advance it through the back-link phase and delete it on completion.

New `resumeMerge()` reads the sentinel, computes which phases remain via the step index, and executes only those — producing the same final vault state as an uninterrupted merge. A `__crashAfter` test hook enables deterministic crash simulation at each phase boundary.

### Backend interface (`src/lib/backend.ts`)

Added `findCommentByMarker(taskPage, marker)` to the `Backend` interface. Implemented in all three backends: Asana searches stories via `getStories`, Jira searches comments via `getComments`, GitHub uses `gh issue view --json comments`. The marker format is `<!-- rubber-ducky:merge:<asanaRef>+<jiraRef> -->`.

### Writeback executor (`src/lib/writeback.ts`)

Added `onPreAction` hook to `runWriteActions` — called before each write action with the resolved backend. If it returns `{ skip: true }`, the action is recorded as a success without hitting the remote. This decouples idempotency logic from the executor.

### Merge command (`src/commands/merge.ts`)

New `--resume` and `--abort` flags. The resume path calls `resumeMerge`, then completes the back-link phase with idempotency checks. The abort path shows remaining work, confirms with the user (TTY) or requires `--yes` (JSON), and deletes the sentinel.

The back-link phase now tracks per-backend posted status in the sentinel, so a crash between Asana and Jira back-link posts only retries the one that didn't complete.

### Shared command guard (`src/commands/shared.ts`)

Extracted `guardOrphanSentinel(workspaceRoot, jsonMode)` — the single implementation of the preflight check used by merge, migrate, and ingest. Produces consistent TTY and JSON diagnostics with operation, step, refs, and exact resolution commands.

### Doctor check (`src/lib/doctor.ts`)

New `checkStaleSentinels` check — error severity for sentinels with `lastUpdated` older than 24 hours. Fresh sentinels (in-progress operations) pass. Finding text includes the exact `--resume` / `--abort` commands.

### Workspace init (`src/lib/workspace.ts`, `src/lib/templates.ts`)

`.rubber-ducky/transactions/` added to workspace directory structure (created by `init` and `migrate`). `.rubber-ducky/` added to the generated `.gitignore` — sentinels are local state, not vault content.

### Per-file atomicity gap (`src/lib/vault-rewrite.ts`)

Documented in a JSDoc comment that per-file wikilink writes are not atomic (no temp+rename). Operation-level resumability covers the broader case; per-file atomicity is deferred to a follow-up.

## Migration notes

No migrations or env changes needed. Existing workspaces gain the transactions directory on next `init` or `migrate` run; its absence doesn't break anything — the directory is created lazily on first sentinel write.

## Test plan

- [x] `merge-sentinel.test.ts` — 27 tests: write/read round-trip, advance, delete, abort, listing, staleness, orphan detection, corrupted sentinel handling, schema version rejection, remaining work descriptions, history log
- [x] `merge-resume.test.ts` — 18 tests: crash at each phase leaves sentinel at expected step, resume from each phase produces consistent vault state, abort deletes sentinel with diagnostics, partially-posted back-links resume correctly, transaction history tracks crash+resume cycles
- [x] `merge.test.ts` — updated existing tests for sentinel on MergeSuccess, idempotency marker in comment text
- [x] `asana-backend.test.ts` — 4 new tests for `findCommentByMarker` (found, not found, ignores system stories, no reference)
- [x] `jira-backend.test.ts` — 3 new tests for `findCommentByMarker`
- [x] `doctor.test.ts` — 3 new tests: no sentinels, fresh sentinel passes, stale sentinel fails with resolution commands
- [x] `workspace.test.ts` — 2 new tests: transactions dir created, `.rubber-ducky/` in gitignore
- [x] Full suite: 1,244 tests across 53 files, all passing
- [ ] Manual: run `rubber-ducky merge ECOMM-X WEB-Y`, Ctrl-C mid-run, verify sentinel exists, run `--resume`, verify vault is consistent
- [ ] Manual: run `rubber-ducky merge --abort` after an interrupted merge, verify sentinel deleted and diagnostic printed

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

Two bugs were preventing the web app from showing sensor values even after the previous fix in PR #4.

## Root Cause 1 — `MainForm.cs`: initial hardware update ran before hardware was enabled

`_computer.Accept(_updateVisitor)` was called at line 187, immediately after `_computer.Open()`. At that point, all hardware-enable flags (`IsCpuEnabled`, `IsMotherboardEnabled`, etc.) are still `false` — so `Open()` adds no hardware groups and the update does nothing.

The actual enabling happens later, at lines 259–287, where `UserOption` objects are created for each hardware category. **`UserOption.Changed` fires immediately when a handler is registered** (see `UserOption.cs` lines 55–57). So `_computer.IsCpuEnabled = true`, etc., all trigger *after* the initial update had already run on an empty computer.

**Fix**: Move `_computer.Accept(_updateVisitor)` to just after the last hardware-enabling `UserOption` registration (after line 287). By then, all hardware groups have been added and `HardwareNode`/`SensorNode` objects exist — so the update activates sensors and sets their values before the web server can serve its first `data.json` request.

## Root Cause 2 — `ohm_web.js`: refresh broke `parent` references

`viewModel.update` called:
```js
ko.mapping.fromJS(data, {}, viewModel);
```
The empty `{}` options bypassed the `Children.create` function responsible for constructing `node` instances with their `parent` property. Refreshed child nodes had `parent = undefined`, causing a `TypeError` on `parent.id()` in the HTML binding — silently breaking all manual and auto-refresh functionality.

**Fix**: Extract a `makeMappingOptions(parent)` helper and use it in both the `node` constructor and `viewModel.update`, ensuring refreshed nodes are always proper `node` instances with correct `parent` references.

## Changes

- **`LibreHardwareMonitor/UI/MainForm.cs`**: Remove `_computer.Accept(_updateVisitor)` from line 187; re-add it after all hardware-enabling `UserOption` setups (after line 287).
- **`LibreHardwareMonitor/Resources/Web/js/ohm_web.js`**: Extract `makeMappingOptions(parent)` helper; use it in `node` constructor and `viewModel.update`.

author: rupakm
body:
## Summary

Two-part refactor of the atomic Paxos model: (1) decouple safety
predicates from proposer bookkeeping via a ghost `voted` field, and
(2) add a guarded proposer crash action for Phase 1 failures.

Depends on PR #21 (faithful Paxos bounded-unrolling wrapper).

## Phase A: acceptor-side safeAt (commit 20b5d52)

Adds `voted : Fin n → Nat → Option Value` ghost field to `PaxosState`.
Reformulates `votedFor`, `wontVoteAt`, `safeAt` to reference only
`voted` and `prom` (no more `did2b`/`prop`). Adds 6 linking invariants
to `PaxosInv` (hL, hK, hN, hAcc, hM, hVotDid). Re-proves init/p1b/p2a/
p2b preservation + agreement. Threads the new field through
`BoundedPaxos.lean`'s tightness construction.

- Paxos.lean: 811 → 1022 lines (+211)
- BoundedPaxos.lean: 1184 → 1250 lines (+66)

## Phase B: guarded proposer crash (commit ad0fa42)

Adds `crashState c s` (reset `got1b c`, `rep c`) with guard
`prop c = none`. Proves all 15 `PaxosInv` fields preserved. Key lemma:
`did2b_false_of_prop_none` — under the invariant, an uncommitted
proposer has no accept records, making all proposer-referencing fields
vacuous for the crashed proposer.

Defines `ExtendedReachable` (init + normal steps + crashes) and proves
`extended_agreement`.

- BoundedPaxos.lean: 1250 → 1451 lines (+201)

## Why Phase 1 only

The 15-field `PaxosInv` creates a tight coupling:
- `hJ: prop q ≠ none → majority(got1b q)` — can't reset `got1b` with
  stable `prop`
- `hL: voted → ∃ q, prop q = some v` — can't reset `prop` (witness loss)
- `hG: did2b ∧ got1b → rep = some _` — can't reset `rep` with stable
  `got1b`

The guard `prop c = none` sidesteps all three. Post-Phase-2a proposer
crash (where `prop c ≠ none`) is infeasible without deeper invariant
restructuring.

The message-passing model (PR #22) handles the general case: its
invariant never references proposer state, so crashes are trivially
safe regardless of proposer phase.

## Verification

- `lake build`: 256/256 green
- 0 sorries across both modified files
- Standard axioms only
- `agreement` and `boundedPaxos_bound_tight` statements unchanged

## Test plan

- [x] `lake build` passes
- [x] 0 sorries
- [x] `extended_agreement` proved for crash-extended reachability
- [x] `boundedPaxos_agreement` and `boundedPaxos_bound_tight` unchanged

body:
## Description

Closes #152

Adds `VertexRagRetrievalTool`, a new built-in tool that grounds model responses using a Vertex AI RAG corpus. Mirrors the pattern established by `GoogleSearchTool` — it modifies the LLM request config server-side via `processLlmRequest` and requires no local execution.

### Key design decisions

- **One tool = one corpus**: The Vertex AI RAG Engine backend only supports one corpus per `ragResources` array. Users who need multiple corpora should create multiple tool instances.
- **Follows `GoogleSearchTool` pattern**: Extends `BaseTool`, overrides `processLlmRequest`, `runAsync` is a no-op.

author: brainlid
body:
## Problem

When a tool invocation spawns a long-running side-effect (such as a sub-agent running as a child process), the tool implementation has no ergonomic way to correlate that side-effect back to the originating `tool_call_id`. This matters for cancellation: if a sub-agent is cancelled mid-flight, the caller needs the `tool_call_id` to update the corresponding tool call's status in the conversation history. Today, the only way to get it is to thread it through the tool's JSON arguments, which pollutes the schema visible to the LLM and relies on the model to round-trip a value it shouldn't need to reason about.

## Solution

`LLMChain.execute_tool_call/3` now enriches the `context` map passed to `Function.execute/3` with the current `tool_call_id` under the `:tool_call_id` key, before the tool runs. The `context` map is the conventional carrier for invocation-scoped metadata that tools can read but the LLM never sees, so this is the natural place for it.

The merge handles three cases defensively:

- `nil` context — a fresh `%{tool_call_id: call.call_id}` map is created
- map context — `:tool_call_id` is added via `Map.put/3`, preserving any keys the caller already set
- any other shape — passed through unchanged, preserving backward compatibility for non-map contexts

Tool implementations that don't care about the `tool_call_id` are unaffected.

## Changes

- `lib/chains/llm_chain.ex` — In `execute_tool_call/3`, build an `enriched_context` that includes `:tool_call_id` and pass it to `Function.execute/3` instead of the raw `context`

## Testing

No new tests were added for this change directly. The enrichment is straightforward (a three-branch merge before an existing call site) and the behaviour is exercised indirectly by any test that runs a tool through `LLMChain`. The main consumer of this new capability — sub-agent cancellation — will carry its own tests when that work lands.

body:
The current pix2pix generator had size/channel inconsistencies across bottleneck and decoder skip connections, causing shape-related runtime failures during forward passes. This update aligns spatial and channel dimensions through the full U-Net path so concatenations and final projection are dimensionally valid.

- **Generator bottleneck shape consistency**
  - Updated bottleneck convolution to preserve expected 4×4 spatial resolution before decoder upsampling.

- **Decoder skip-connection channel alignment**
  - Corrected decoder block input channel definitions to match actual concatenated tensors:
    - `dec3`: `base_filters*12`
    - `dec2`: `base_filters*6`
    - `dec1`: `base_filters*3`

- **Final projection channel fix**
  - Updated final output conv input channels to match `dec1` concatenated with original RGB input:
    - `nn.Conv2d(base_filters + in_channels, out_channels, ...)`

```python
# Decoder channels after skip concatenation
self.dec3 = DeconvBlock(base_filters*12, base_filters*4)
self.dec2 = DeconvBlock(base_filters*6, base_filters*2)
self.dec1 = DeconvBlock(base_filters*3, base_filters)

# Final projection from [dec1 || input]
self.final = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Conv2d(base_filters + in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size=1, stride=1, padding=0),
    nn.Tanh()
)
```

body:
## What this PR does

This PR formalizes OBS-043 as a first-class observatory layer.

Main changes:

- renames `experiments/studies/fim_response_flow.py` to:
  - `experiments/studies/obs043_response_flow.py`
- adds the repository-facing canonical object note:
  - `docs/05_project/canonical_response_guided_flow.md`

## Why this matters

OBS-043 is now more than an exploratory script result.

It introduces a genuine observatory layer extension:
- the dominant response eigenvector field defines a structured local direction law
- embedded integration yields a seam-engaged dynamical flow picture
- relaxed integration reveals broader response-guided routing
- seam-bundle mismatch scalars modulate routing without collapsing seam engagement

This PR aligns the repository with that scientific status.

## Scope

This PR is intentionally narrow.

It does:
- promote the response-flow study into OBS-numbered naming
- add a canonical repository-facing definition of response-guided flow

It does **not**:
- add the path-family companion study yet
- change canonical seam-family artifacts
- promote response-flow code into `src/pam/`
- introduce continuous-flow reconstruction

## Canonical object added

The new document defines **response-guided flow** as:

- a dominant response-eigenvector direction field
- a path-local orientation rule
- a forward-admissible embedded step relation
- a score-based discrete integration rule
- a family of discrete integral-like trajectories on the manifold graph

It also records:
- key observables
- empirical stabilization from OBS-043
- current methodological limitations
- relation to future work

## Why the rename is important

The old name `fim_response_flow.py` reflected an exploratory phase.

The new name `obs043_response_flow.py` reflects that this study now belongs to the canonical observatory sequence and has produced a stable enough result to be logged as OBS-043.

## Reviewer guidance

Please review this PR as:
- the repository formalization of OBS-043,
- and as the point where response-guided flow becomes a named observatory object rather than only an experiment script.

author: xukp20
body: > Reroll of #511 on top of the latest upstream `main`. Functional scope is unchanged; this PR is only refreshed to bring it back to the top of the review queue. # Progress Card Compression, Runtime Style Switching, and `/progress` Timeline Review ## Summary This PR improves long-running task observability in `cc-connect`, with a focus on the `Feishu + Codex` workflow. It covers two connected improvements: 1. Better progress rendering for long tasks 2. A new `/progress` command for reviewing recent progress timelines after a reply completes The main goals are: - reduce visual noise in long `thinking / tool use / tool result` sequences - make `Feishu` progress cards practical as the default experience - allow runtime switching between `legacy / compact / card` without editing config files - preserve recent assistant-turn progress events so users can inspect them after the final reply ## Motivation The existing progress experience had two main gaps: 1. Long-running tasks produced too much vertical noise, especially when `tool use` and `tool result` were always split into separate blocks. 2. Once progress content was truncated or rolled out of the live card window, there was no convenient way to inspect the previous events for the latest assistant reply. This PR addresses both: - it makes live progress more configurable and more compact - it adds a timeline model plus `/progress` so recent process events can be reviewed after the fact ## Design ### 1. Progress rendering defaults and runtime controls This PR keeps the existing display controls: - `thinking_max_len` - `tool_max_len` - `tool_messages` and adds new progress-oriented controls: - `progress_style` - `tool_layout` - `tool_show_input` - `tool_show_result_body` - `progress_max_entries` - `progress_history_turns` The intent is: - `progress_style` - runtime-selectable `legacy | compact | card | auto` - `auto` follows the platform default - `tool_layout` - `split` keeps separate tool-use and tool-result blocks - `merged` keeps a single block per tool invocation and upgrades it when the result arrives - `tool_show_input` - controls whether tool input is shown - `tool_show_result_body` - controls whether tool result output is shown - `progress_max_entries` - limits the live recent-window shown in compact/card progress - `progress_history_turns` - controls how many assistant turns keep persisted progress timelines for `/progress` ### 2. Platform defaults This PR keeps progress semantics global, but allows platform defaults to remain platform-specific. Current default behavior after this change: - `Feishu` - default `progress_style = card` - other platforms - continue to use their own platform defaults / existing behavior ### 3. Event timeline persistence Each assistant reply can now keep a corresponding event timeline: - `thinking` - `tool use` - `tool result` These are stored per session in a lightweight `EventTimeline` structure and linked back to the corresponding assistant message via `AssistantHistoryIdx`. This design keeps the existing `History` model intact and adds process history as a parallel structure rather than rewriting message history itself. ### 4. `/progress` This PR adds `/progress` for reviewing recent progress history. Supported forms: - `/progress` - `/progress prev` - `/progress 2` - `/progress prev 2:4` Behavior: - default: latest assistant-turn timeline - `prev`: previous assistant-turn timeline - single numeric selector: one event - `a:b`: event range The command reuses the same layout rules as live progress: - `merged / split` - input visibility - result-body visibility - card vs text style So `/progress` and live progress stay aligned. ## Supported User-Facing Behavior ### Runtime configuration These can now be changed in chat via `/config`: ```text /config set progress_style legacy /config set progress_style compact /config set progress_style card /config set progress_style auto /config set tool_layout merged /config set tool_layout split /config set tool_show_input true /config set tool_show_result_body false /config set progress_max_entries 20 /config set progress_history_turns 3 ``` ### Live progress For `Feishu`, the recommended default experience is: - interactive progress card - `tool_layout = merged` - tool input visible - tool result body visible This reduces duplication while keeping enough detail to audit what actually ran. ### Historical review After a reply completes, users can inspect recent process events with `/progress` without rerunning the task. ## Examples ### Example prompt used in live validation ```text 请只做两步，不要修改文件。 1. 读取 docs/usage.zh-CN.md 的前 10 行。 2. 再执行 cat does-not-exist.txt。 ``` This single example is useful because it covers: - a successful read - a failed command - mixed progress events - card rendering - `/progress` replay behavior ### Screenshot plan #### 1. `merged` Use: ```text /config set tool_layout merged ``` Then run the prompt above and capture the resulting `Feishu` card. #### 2. `split` Use: ```text /config set tool_layout split ``` Then run the same prompt and capture the resulting `Feishu` card. These two screenshots are enough to demonstrate: - the new default direction - the `merged / split` contrast - successful and failed tool rendering in the same example ## Code Changes ### Configuration and runtime controls - `config/config.go` - extends display config with progress-specific options - persists runtime display updates - `cmd/cc-connect/main.go` - wires config values into runtime display state - `config.example.toml` - documents the new progress-related settings ### Engine and event capture - `core/engine.go` - extends runtime `/config` items - captures progress events during `processInteractiveEvents(...)` - appends timelines when assistant replies complete - adds `/progress` - `core/session.go` - adds timeline persistence to session state - `core/event_timeline.go` - defines `EventTimeline` and `TimelineEvent` ### Progress rendering - `core/progress_compact.go` - adds runtime `progress_style` override support - adds `merged` tool-block behavior - makes recent-window size configurable - keeps `/progress` rendering aligned with live progress rules - `platform/feishu/feishu.go` - keeps `Feishu` default progress style as `card` - updates progress entry rendering - supports progress-payload replies for `/progress` ### `/progress` - `core/progress_command.go` - parses latest/previous/single/range selectors - renders either card payloads or text fallback depending on style ### Docs and i18n - `core/i18n.go` - adds help / labels / progress-related command text - `docs/usage.zh-CN.md` - documents config and `/progress` - `docs/feishu.md` - documents `Feishu` defaults and style behavior ## Local Testing Completed locally: ```bash go build ./... go test ./... -count=1 go test -race ./... ``` Additional focused verification was also run during iteration for: - `core` - `platform/feishu` - merged tool-block behavior - `/progress` rendering and selection - progress payload handling in Feishu replies ## Live Feishu Validation Live validation was completed against `Feishu + Codex`. Validated areas: - `Feishu` default `progress_style = card` - runtime switching: - `legacy` - `compact` - `card` - `auto` - `merged / split` - `tool_show_result_body = fa

author: pedropacheco95
body:
## Ticket
[PAD-10](https://linear.app/padellevelup/issue/PAD-10/class-deletion-ui-not-updating-shows-false-error-message)

## What changed
When deleting a recurring class's single occurrence, `_remove_single_occurrence_from_lesson` calls `split_lesson()` (which commits DB changes) and then `schedule_lesson_reminder_jobs()`. If the scheduler threw an exception, the endpoint returned HTTP 500 even though the deletion had already persisted — causing a false "Delete failed" toast in the UI and requiring a manual refresh.

Wrapped the post-deletion scheduler calls in try-except in both `_remove_single_occurrence_from_lesson` and `_truncate_lesson_future` so that scheduler failures never mask a successful deletion.

## Files changed
- `padel_app/services/lesson_service.py` — try-except around `schedule_lesson_reminder_jobs` and `cancel_lesson_reminder_jobs` calls

## Testing
- E2E test: `levelup_frontend/e2e/schedule-calendar/class-deletion.spec.ts`
  - Non-recurring class deletion shows success toast
  - Recurring class single-occurrence deletion shows success toast

## Summary

- Add `tools/auto-promote.sh` — external cron script that evaluates per-agent fitness from experience data and decides when to promote (confidence step-up) or evolve (`.ag` source mutation)
- Add `tools/auto-promote-config.yaml` — configurable decision rules (promote prerequisites, evolve triggers, dry-run flag)
- All 5 safety guards from #148: federation-running check, lock file, confidence-seeded check, PID liveness, dry-run default ON

## Decision rules

**Promote** (0.5→0.6→0.85): min 200 entries, 48h runtime, reject rate <5%, non-negative delta slope.
**Evolve**: negative slope over 1000 entries OR reject rate >20%.

## Safety

1. `agentis daemon list --json` empty → exit 0
2. `tools/.auto-promote.lock` prevents overlapping cron runs
3. Per-agent confidence null check (skips unseeded agents)
4. `kill -0 PID` before acting on a daemon
5. `dry_run: true` by default — all actions logged but not executed

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `tools/auto-promote.sh` | Main script (bash, uses python3 for YAML parsing + decision evaluation) |
| `tools/auto-promote-config.yaml` | Default config with all thresholds |

author: xukp20
body:
> Reroll of #379 on top of the latest upstream `main`. Functional scope is unchanged; this PR is only refreshed to bring it back to the top of the review queue.

## Summary

  Add a reset-only `/clear` command for the current session.

  This implements the original request from #354: clear the current session context in place without creating a new session entry like `/new`.

  ## What changed

  - add `/clear` as a first-class command
  - keep the current logical session and active session slot unchanged
  - clear local history for the current session
  - detach the current backend agent session binding
  - clean up the current interactive state so the next message starts a fresh backend session
  - add regression tests for:
    - clearing the current session in place
    - preserving the current session identity/name
    - workspace-scoped `/clear`
    - invalid `/clear` usage
  - update i18n strings and usage docs

  ## Why

  Today, the only way to start fresh is `/new`, which creates a brand new session.

  That makes `/list` grow quickly even in cases where the user does not want a new logical session, and only wants to clear the current conversation context while keeping the same session identity.

  This PR addresses the original feature request in #354.

  Maintainer context on #354:
  - the feature was already acknowledged and marked as planned with P2 priority

  ## Scope decision

  While implementing `/clear`, I also evaluated whether cc-connect should support a native clear path in the underlying CLI session.

  That native path is intentionally **not included** in this PR.

  Reasons:

  1. Codex native slash commands are not reliable enough in `exec/resume --json` mode
     Related investigation: #378

     In particular:
     - `/clear` is not behaviorally reliable in direct Codex CLI testing
     - `/compact` also does not appear stable enough to treat as a guaranteed native capability in the current integration mode

  2. Claude Code native `/clear` should be validated separately before exposing it in cc-connect
     Claude Code does support native slash commands in general, but `/clear` behavior in the current cc-connect integration path still needs separate validation, including Claude-side session/control semantics.

  Because of that, this PR keeps the implementation conservative:
  - `/clear` only resets the session at the cc-connect layer
  - it reuses the same cc-connect logical session
  - it achieves a “fresh start” by dropping the old backend session binding and starting a new backend session on the next user message

  ## Validation

  - [x] `go build ./...`
  - [x] `go test ./... -v -race`
  - [x] `go test ./... -coverprofile=coverage.out -covermode=atomic`
  - [x] `$(go env GOPATH)/bin/staticcheck ./...`
  - [x] `$(go env GOPATH)/bin/actionlint -color`

  ## Related issues

  - Fixes #354
  - Related investigation for Codex slash-command reliability: #378

body:
## Summary

This PR contains L2CAP PTS test enhancements and a critical GATT indication use-after-free fix.

### GATT: Fix indication use-after-free on async data

`bt_gatt_indicate()` is asynchronous (waits for peer confirmation), but `params->data` pointed to `req->value` which gets freed by `sal_invoke_async()` after the worker returns. The indication would then send already-freed memory data.

**Fix:** Allocate a separate heap copy of the indication data, free it in `send_indication_destory()` callback. Also added parameter validation for `send_notification` and `send_indication` entry functions.

### L2CAP: PTS test command enhancements

- Add `echo`, `brconfig`, `brwrite`, `brdisconnect` commands for BR/EDR L2CAP PTS testing
- Add `sec_level` parameter to `listen` command
- Add `CONFIG_BT_L2CAP_SEG_RECV` segmented receive support
- Add encryption key size check in server accept callback (BV-15-C)
- Add single channel per PSM restriction for PTS (BV-17-C)
- Remove `mps > mtu` validation (valid per spec)
- Remove 48-byte brwrite data length limit
- Skip pipe connect for BR/EDR transport channels

### SPP fixes

- Add SDP discover timeout and fix resource cleanup
- Fix resource leak when RFCOMM connect fails after SDP

## Test

- L2CAP PTS test cases (BV-12-C, BV-15-C, BV-17-C, etc.)
- GATT indication/notification functional test

### Motivation
- Introduce robust multi-tenant handling for public invite links and owner-portal login flows so a `tid` can be propagated and tenant DB prefixes are normalized.
- Make the dispatcher and cron tenant context explicit and add safer prefix generation and logging to avoid invalid table names.
- Improve appointment reminder delivery semantics to ensure owner reminders are required and to report skipped items.

### Description
- Added `prefixFromTid()` to normalize `tid` values into prefixes (e.g. `praxis-wenzel` -> `t_praxis_wenzel_`) and applied it in `CronController::dispatcher()` with additional cron logging. 
- Updated the calendar reminder flow in `ReminderService::processPending()` to skip appointments with missing owner email, track `skipped`, and only mark reminders sent after successful owner-send; adjusted `AppointmentRepository::findPendingReminders()` time window and email conditions.
- Propagated tenant `tid` into owner-portal pages and actions by storing a `portal_tenant_prefix` in session, added ambiguity detection in `findUserAcrossAllTenants()` to block logins when an email exists in multiple tenants, and threaded `tid` through redirects and forms in `OwnerAuthController` and templates.
- Owner-portal mails now include the `?tid=` query when appropriate via `OwnerPortalMailService::tenantQuery()` and `getBaseUrl()` adjustments.
- Reworked patient-invite handling to build invite URLs with `?tid=`, to apply tenant context on landing/submit/test/thankyou actions via `applyTenantContextForToken()`, and to locate the correct tenant table when no `tid` query param is provided by searching `information_schema` tables.
- Minor templates changes: added hidden `tid` inputs to `owner_login.twig` and `owner_set_password.twig` and included `tid` in form actions.

### Testing
- Performed automated PHP syntax checks on all modified files using `php -l` and confirmed no syntax errors.
- No changes to existing unit tests were made and the project test suite was not executed as part of this rollout.

author: saihgupr
body:
### 🚨 Severity: MEDIUM

### 💡 Vulnerability
Unbounded user input in the `searchQuery` field was allowed to grow without limits. While this is primarily user-controlled input, large inputs processed via `localizedCaseInsensitiveContains` can cause the Main Thread to hang, creating a localized Denial of Service (DoS) for the application. Furthermore, passing unbounded query text to the Gemini API (`parseSearchIntent`) could lead to excessive token usage, billing abuse, or external API DoS vectors if the service is programmatically triggered.

### 🎯 Impact
*   **Local DoS:** Extremely large input strings would cause severe application lag when calculating string operations synchronously in `ContentView`.
*   **Token Exhaustion:** Sending unbounded inputs to the AI API increases billing costs and risks hitting hard token limits on the external provider.

### 🔧 Fix
1.  **UI Defense:** Modified the `.onChange(of: searchQuery)` modifier in `ContentView.swift` to enforce a 2000-character limit using `newValue.count`, truncating any excess.
2.  **API Defense-in-Depth:** Updated `GeminiService.swift` to apply a `.prefix(2000)` truncation to the query parameter before inserting it into the prompt JSON body, ensuring the backend never attempts to process massive strings.

### ✅ Verification
1.  Paste a block of text larger than 2000 characters into the search field. The application will instantly truncate it to 2000 characters without crashing or hanging.
2.  Triggering an AI Search with the long text ensures the API payload remains within expected boundaries.

author: zaifastafa
body:
## Summary

When the admin sidebar is collapsed and a menu entry near the bottom of the sidebar is hovered, the flyout submenu extends beyond the viewport. This makes entries at the bottom of the flyout inaccessible since there is no way to scroll them into view.

**Changes:**
- Calculate a dynamic `max-height` for the flyout based on the remaining viewport space below its top position
- Add `overflow-y: auto` to enable vertical scrolling when content exceeds the available height
- Add test coverage for the new `max-height` style

## How to reproduce

1. Collapse the admin sidebar
2. Install enough plugins or modules to have a long submenu (e.g., Settings)
3. Hover over a menu entry near the bottom of the sidebar
4. Observe the flyout extends below the viewport

## How to verify

After this fix, the flyout constrains itself to the remaining viewport height and becomes scrollable.

author: joshuamoelans
body:
The poller silently ignored commit-status failures (e.g. console compat checks) because the failure branch only checked for unsuccessful check runs. This left publish issues stuck as ci-pending with no comment. From `sentry-native` we added these checks in our console repos that report back with a commit status (e.g. [sentry-switch](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-switch/actions/runs/24468542398/job/71504743073#step:3:33)) , but since all actual check-runs in [sentry-native CI](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-native/actions/runs/24468536557) passed, the CI status poller doesn't finish since it's waiting for `status_ok` to become true (or some CI check to be unsuccessful, which they are not). ## Analysis The following flowgraph shows the existing paths, and the new path (added in purple). Before, we would just end up in the orange state, stuck in `ci-pending` (see https://github.com/getsentry/publish/issues/7819), since we'd never reach any of the other terminal states. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Start: process issue] --> B{total_checks == 0
AND total_statuses == 0?} B -->|Yes| C[No CI found yet — skip] B -->|No| D{commit_status == success?} D -->|Yes| E[status_ok = true] D -->|No| F{total_statuses == 0?} F -->|Yes| G[status_ok = true
repo uses only check runs] F -->|No| H[status_ok = false] E --> I{status_ok == true
AND pending == 0
AND unsuccessful == 0?} G --> I I -->|Yes| J[✅ CI passed
Add ci-ready label
Comment on issue] I -->|No| K{pending == 0
AND unsuccessful != 0?} H --> K K -->|Yes| L[❌ Check-run failure
Comment with failed check names] K -->|No| N{commit_status == failure
AND pending == 0
AND unsuccessful == 0?} N -->|Yes| P[❌ Commit-status failure
Comment with failed status contexts] N -->|No| M[⏳ Still pending
— silent, retry next tick] style J fill:#2ecc71,stroke:#27ae60,color:#fff style L fill:#e74c3c,stroke:#c0392b,color:#fff style M fill:#f39c12,stroke:#e67e22,color:#fff style C fill:#95a5a6,stroke:#7f8c8d,color:#fff style P fill:#9b59b6,stroke:#6c3483,color:#fff,stroke-width:4px style N fill:#d2b4de,stroke:#6c3483,color:#000,stroke-width:3px linkStyle 13 stroke:#9b59b6,stroke-width:3px linkStyle 14 stroke:#9b59b6,stroke-width:3px ```

author: rebaunana
body:
The homevideos collection type playback query was hardcoded to only include Photos (MediaTypes: 'Photo'), causing Shuffle and Play All to fail with NO_MEDIA_ERROR when the library contains videos.

Changed to 'Photo,Video' so both media types are included in the playback queue.

Fixes jellyfin-web#7176

<!--
Ensure your title is short, descriptive, and in the imperative mood (Fix X, Change Y, instead of Fixed X, Changed Y).
For a good inspiration of what to write in commit messages and PRs please review https://chris.beams.io/posts/git-commit/ and our https://jellyfin.org/docs/general/contributing/issues page.
-->

### Changes
  The homevideos collection type playback query in playbackmanager.js was
  hardcoded to only fetch items with MediaTypes: 'Photo'. This caused Shuffle   
  and Play All to fail with PlaybackError.NO_MEDIA_ERROR when the library
  contains videos, because the query returned zero playable items.              
                  
  Changed MediaTypes: 'Photo' to MediaTypes: 'Photo,Video' so both media types  
  are included in the playback queue. Individual video playback was not affected
   because it bypasses translateItemsForPlayback() entirely. 

### Issues
  Fixes #7176  

### Code assistance
  Claude Code was used to trace the bug through the minified bundle back to the 
  source, identifying the hardcoded MediaTypes: 'Photo' filter at line 1941 as
  the root cause.

author: arimendelow
body:
## What shipped
- exported a shared credential error sanitizer from `bitwarden-store.ts` and routed `credential_store` through it, so agent-saved secret flows now scrub failures the same way provider auth does
- taught the shared sanitizer to strip raw `Command failed: bw ...` lines, hidden prompt echoes like `[input is hidden]`, shorter encoded payload blobs, and secret-shaped values, while collapsing fully scrubbed failures back to plain `command failed`
- added regression coverage for the shared sanitizer itself plus the `credential_store` path that agents hit after signups and manual secret saves
- bumped the releasable package versions together to `0.1.0-alpha.407` so the CLI and `ouro.bot` wrapper can ship this secret-save hardening cleanly

## Why this matters
After the auth fixes in #521, the agent-facing `credential_store` path was still keeping its own little error scrubber. That meant provider auth could fail cleanly while agent-saved secrets after a signup could still drift into their own weird command-shaped mess. Secret writes should fail in one consistent dialect across the harness.

## How to try it yourself
1. Use any family-trusted flow that ends with `credential_store`, such as signing up for a site and then storing the accepted password.
2. Force the underlying vault write to fail.
3. Confirm the returned tool error no longer echoes raw `bw` command text, hidden prompt lines, or encoded payload blobs.

## Verification
- `npm test -- --run src/__tests__/repertoire/credential-error-sanitizer.test.ts src/__tests__/repertoire/tools-credential.test.ts src/__tests__/repertoire/bitwarden-store.test.ts`
- `npm test -- --run src/__tests__/heart/versioning/wrapper-publish-guard.test.ts src/__tests__/scripts/changelog-gate.test.ts`
- `npx tsc --noEmit`
- `npm run test:coverage`

## Live agent validation
- encoded the exact raw `bw create item ...` plus hidden prompt echo failure shape in the `credential_store` regression tests
- verified the shared sanitizer still preserves the Bitwarden-specific locked-session classification in the real store tests
- did not run a live secret-saving signup against production vault credentials in this worktree; the validation path here is test-first and shaped around the observed failure modes

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Implement a centrally managed remote content/config system for the app so that published App Store builds can be updated without a new binary for approved data-driven changes.

## Goals
Add support for fetching and applying a remote JSON config that can control:
- weekly/game-event settings such as current challenge mode/rotation
- theme colors and visual presets
- IntroHub background image/overlay
- music and sound pack selection/URLs
- AI player avatar/profile overrides
- main TV announcement messages

## Requirements
1. Create a typed remote config model and loader.
2. Load the remote config at app startup, cache it locally, and fall back to built-in defaults if the network fails.
3. Apply remote theme values to the existing app shell / document body where appropriate.
4. Add support for IntroHub background and message overrides from remote config.
5. Add support for AI player avatar/profile overrides from remote config.
6. Add support for main TV announcement/message overrides from remote config.
7. Add support for audio pack selection / remote music URLs in the existing sound system, without introducing remote code execution.
8. Make challenge scheduling able to honor a remote weekly challenge override (for example, QuickTap-only week) using data-driven config rather than hardcoded client changes.
9. Preserve existing behavior when remote config is absent or invalid.
10. Keep all changes compatible with the current TypeScript/React/Redux codebase and existing app startup flow.

## Constraints / Notes
- Remote config must be treated strictly as data, not executable code.
- Use existing app patterns where possible (Redux slices, startup hydration, service modules).
- Prefer minimal invasive changes and safe fallbacks.
- If there are existing concepts for theme, IntroHub, AI player profiles, TV feed, or audio settings, integrate with them instead of duplicating state.
- Add any necessary types, selectors, helpers, and tests for the new behavior.

## Suggested implementation direction
- Add a `remoteConfig` or similar slice/service.
- Fetch a JSON document from a configurable endpoint (with a default path and optional env override if supported by the app).
- Merge remote values into existing settings/content at runtime.
- Ensure app remains functional offline using existing defaults.

## Expected outcome
A user can update the remote JSON configuration centrally and have App Store users receive new weekly challenge settings, theme/content updates, player profile images, and announcement text without shipping a new app binary.

The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated):

User: when i package my game as an app and publish to the app store can i still manage it centrally via github? meaning if i make a change in github let's say a quicktap race week, where all week every challenge is quickatp will that refelect on the app or how does it work how can i manage it centrally

Assistant: Yes — you can manage a published app centrally via GitHub **if the app is designed to fetch its live content/config from your backend or a remote source**.  

But if the change is **baked into the app build** itself, then **publishing a new GitHub commit does not automatically update the App Store app**. Users would only get the change after you:

1. update the code in GitHub,
2. build a new iOS app binary,
3. submit it to the App Store,
4. and the update is approved and installed by users.

## The key distinction

### 1) Code changes
Examples:
- game logic
- UI layout
- new screens
- minigame behavior
- challenge rules hardcoded in the client

These require a **new app release** if they live in the shipped app bundle.

### 2) Remote-config / live content changes
Examples:
- “this week all challenges are QuickTap Race”
- featured event of the week
- difficulty multipliers
- seasonal schedule
- reward tables
- daily challenge rotations

These can be changed centrally **without App Store resubmission** if the app loads them from:
- your Express server
- a JSON config file hosted remotely
- a CMS or admin endpoint
- Firebase/Supabase/other backend
- GitHub-hosted data that your server reads from

## So for your example
> “quicktap race week, where all week every challenge is quicktap”

That **can reflect in the app immediately** if the app is built to read challenge rotation from a central source at runtime.

If instead the week’s challenge list is defined directly in React/TypeScript source and compiled into the app, then **no**, publishing a GitHub change alone will not update the installed app.

## Best practice for central management
Use a **hybrid model**:

### Ship in the app
- core game engine
- UI
- rendering
- validation logic
- fallback/default content

### Keep remote
- weekly challenge schedule
- featured modes
- event flags
- balancing values
- seasonal content
- copy/text
- onboarding messages

author: eazyaccessea
body:
## Description

Introduces Allowance Guard's marketing managed-agent system: a coordinated set of 12 Claude Code skills under `.claude/skills/` that orchestrate research, positioning, content strategy, SEO, writing, social media, outreach, conversion optimization, analytics, imagery direction, campaign management, and web implementation.

The system is governed by the Standing Council and sub-councils (defined in `memory/PROCESS.md`), backed by scoped memory in `memory/marketing/`, and fenced by deny rules in `.claude/settings.json` to prevent accidental mutations to payment, auth, DB, or API code.

**Key additions:**

- **12 marketing skills** (each with a `SKILL.md` spec):
  - `market-research` — competitive + audience research
  - `positioning` — message selection for segments
  - `content-strategy` — editorial calendar planning
  - `seo` — keyword research + SERP briefs
  - `writer` — long-form prose (blog, docs, explainers)
  - `social` — X, Farcaster, LinkedIn drafts
  - `outreach` — PECR/GDPR-safe cold email
  - `conversion` — landing page + CTA copy
  - `image-direction` — SVG icons + photoreal prompts
  - `analytics` — aggregated metrics briefs
  - `campaign-manager` — orchestrates all above
  - `web-implementation` — lands approved copy into `src/`

- **Scoped memory** (`memory/marketing/`):
  - `brand.md` — voice, banned phrases, proof standards
  - `audiences.md` — four segments with pains + objections
  - `seo.md` — seven priority keyword clusters
  - `metrics.md` — one primary metric per surface
  - `outreach.md` — target categories + log
  - `imagery.md` — line-art + photoreal canon + prompt library
  - `positioning-history.md`, `content-history.md`, `experiments.md` — append-only logs
  - `MEMORY.md` — index + five standing rules

- **Operational runbook** (`docs/marketing-agents.md`):
  - One principle: educate, clarify, guide; never exaggerate or manipulate fear
  - Team roster with invocation patterns
  - Weekly cycle prompt template
  - Imagery modes (line-art vs. photoreal)

- **Session orientation** (`.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`):
  - Prints load map on session start
  - Points to marketing memory and project docs

- **Safety fences** (`.claude/settings.json`):
  - Deny rules block git push, deploy, DB, Stripe, and destructive commands
  - Allows Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, WebSearch, WebFetch, Bash(git status/diff)

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation update

## Testing

No testing needed. This is a documentation and configuration addition that establishes the marketing agent system structure and operational guidelines. The skills are Claude Code prompts that will be invoked by the user; they do not execute automatically or require unit tests.

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Self-review completed
- [x] Documentation updated (runbook + skill specs + memory index)
- [x] No breaking changes
- [x] No secrets or API keys committed

## Notes

- All skills are read-only or write-to-context by default; `web-implementation` is the only skill that edits `src/` and is fenced to marketing surfaces only.
- The Standing Council gates (defined in `memory/PROCESS.md`) are referenced throughout but not redefined here; they are the governance layer.
- Hard bans (e.g., "Free Forever", "100% free", "No VC") are enforced across all marketing output and mirror the voice rules in `memory/VOICE.md`.
- The weekly cycle is a single prompt to `campaign-manager` that coordinates all specialists and produces drafts only — no publication, send, or site changes without user approval.
