author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Security audit and fixes for critical, high, and medium severity vulnerabilities found in the codebase.

### Changes

**Critical fixes:**
- **Hardcoded JWT secret removed** — `jwt.secret` in `application.properties` and `JwtTokenProvider` no longer contain a hardcoded secret. The secret is now read from `JWT_SECRET` env var. If unset, a random key is generated at startup (with a warning), so dev works out-of-the-box but tokens won't survive restarts.
- **CORS restricted** — `allowedOrigins` changed from `*` to a configurable property (`cors.allowed-origins`), defaulting to `localhost:3000,localhost:8080` for dev. Override via `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` env var in production. Allowed headers restricted to `Authorization`, `Content-Type`, `Accept`. Credentials enabled, preflight max-age set.
- **Swagger gated** — Swagger UI endpoints are now conditionally permitted based on `springdoc.enabled` property (set to `false` in production to hide API docs from unauthenticated users).

**High fixes:**
- **Rate limiting on auth endpoints** — New `RateLimitFilter` limits `/api/auth/**` to 10 requests per minute per IP to mitigate brute-force and mass-registration attacks.
- **CSV file type validation** — Import endpoint now checks content-type and file extension before processing.
- **CORS PATCH method added** — The `/desativar` endpoint uses PATCH, which was missing from the CORS allowed methods list.

**Medium fixes:**
- **CSV formula injection protection** — Import and export now sanitize fields starting with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab, or CR to prevent formula injection when CSV files are opened in spreadsheet applications.

### Files changed
- `SecurityConfig.java` — CORS, Swagger gating, rate limit filter registration
- `JwtTokenProvider.java` — Remove hardcoded secret, random fallback with warning
- `RateLimitFilter.java` — New file, in-memory per-IP rate limiter for auth endpoints
- `CsvController.java` — File type validation on import
- `CsvService.java` — Formula injection sanitization
- `application.properties` — Externalized JWT secret, CORS config, Swagger toggle
- `application-test.properties` — Updated to dedicated test secret
- `JwtTokenProviderTest.java` — Updated to use test-only secret

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify JWT_SECRET is set in production** — The app will generate a random secret if `JWT_SECRET` is not set, meaning tokens won't persist across restarts. Ensure the env var is configured in your deployment.
- [ ] **Verify CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is set in production** — The default only allows localhost. Set this to your actual frontend domain(s).
- [ ] **Verify springdoc.enabled=false in production** — Ensure Swagger UI is disabled in production environments.
- [ ] **Test login/registration rate limiting** — Send >10 requests in 1 minute to `/api/auth/login` and confirm you receive HTTP 429.
- [ ] **Test CSV import with a non-CSV file** — Upload a `.txt` or `.jpg` file and confirm it is rejected with a 400 error.

### Notes
- The rate limiter is in-memory and per-instance. For multi-instance deployments, consider replacing with a Redis-backed solution (e.g., Bucket4j + Redis).
- CSRF remains disabled, which is standard for stateless JWT APIs.
- Open user registration is still allowed — consider adding admin-approval or invite-only registration if this is not desired.
- Password policy only requires 6 characters minimum — consider strengthening this in a follow-up.

body:
## Summary

Add support for responding to Feishu document comments (`drive.notice.comment_add_v1` events) with LLM-powered intelligent replies, including a configurable 3-tier access control system.

### Comment Handler
- Full event orchestration: parse comment event → filter → fetch doc meta + comment details → build timeline → run agent → deliver reply
- Smart timeline selection: local comments (max 20 entries), whole-document comments (max 12 entries)
- Long text chunking (4000 chars) for reply delivery with automatic fallback
- Cross-card session sharing per document (in-memory cache, 50 msg cap, 1h TTL)
- Semantic text extraction (strip @mention noise)
- Document link resolution via `/wiki/v2/spaces/get_node`
- OK reaction indicator while agent is processing

### Tools (5 new)
- `feishu_doc_read` — read document raw content
- `feishu_drive_list_comments` — list document comments
- `feishu_drive_list_comment_replies` — list comment thread replies
- `feishu_drive_reply_comment` — reply to a comment
- `feishu_drive_add_comment` — add a whole-document comment

### 3-Tier Access Control (`feishu_comment_rules.py`)
- **Priority**: exact document rule > wildcard `"*"` rule > top-level config > code defaults
- **Per-field fallback**: `enabled`, `policy`, `allow_from` each resolve independently through the tiers
- **Policies**: `allowlist` (static list only) / `pairing` (static list ∪ runtime-approved store)
- **Explicit-grant only**: every user who triggers a reply must be listed in `allow_from` or in the pairing-approved store — there is no implicit allow-all mode
- **Config**: `~/.hermes/feishu_comment_rules.json`, mtime-cached hot-reload (no restart needed)
- **CLI**: `status` / `check <doc> <user>` / `pairing add|remove|list`

### Event Filtering
- Self-reply filter using generalized `self_open_id` (supports both tenant and future user-identity modes)
- Receiver check: only process events where the bot is the @mentioned target
- Notice type filter: only `add_comment` and `add_reply`

## Files Changed

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `gateway/platforms/feishu_comment.py` | Main comment handler + prompt builders + API layer |
| `gateway/platforms/feishu_comment_rules.py` | 3-tier access control engine + pairing store + CLI |
| `gateway/platforms/feishu.py` | Register comment event handler in adapter |
| `tools/feishu_doc_tool.py` | Document read tool |
| `tools/feishu_drive_tool.py` | 4 drive comment tools |
| `toolsets.py` | Register feishu_doc and feishu_drive toolsets |

## Config Example

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "policy": "pairing",
  "allow_from": ["ou_global_reviewer"],
  "documents": {
    "*": { "policy": "pairing", "allow_from": [] },
    "docx:dxxExxxxxMxxmxxxxxxxx": { "policy": "allowlist", "allow_from": ["ou_doc_owner", "ou_teammate"] }
  }
}
```

## Test Plan

- [x] Allowlist policy: empty allow_from denies all users silently
- [x] Allowlist policy: user in allow_from gets normal reply
- [x] Exact document rule overrides top-level (doc allowlist + narrower allow_from, top pairing)
- [x] Exact document rule overrides wildcard (doc allowlist, wildcard pairing)
- [x] Wildcard rule applies when no exact match
- [x] Pairing policy: unapproved user silently denied
- [x] Pairing policy: CLI `pairing add` grants access immediately (hot-reload)
- [x] Pairing policy: user listed in `allow_from` granted without CLI approval (union semantics)
- [x] Self-reply filter: bot's own comments are skipped
- [x] Receiver filter: comments not @mentioning the bot are skipped

author: fohte
body:
## Purpose

- `fohte/lefthook-config` is only consumed through `generic-boilerplate`, so the indirection no longer earns its keep
- Generated repos pick the runner for prettier/commitlint at runtime, but the template already knows which runner fits from `type` and `monorepo_node_workspace`
    - `lefthook-config` had to probe `bun.lock` / `pnpm-lock.yaml` / `package.json` in shell to stay portable
    - Because of that, changes like pnpm support in `lefthook-config` ripple into every generated repo

## Approach

- Move the lefthook configuration into `template` and stop referencing `fohte/lefthook-config`
- Pick the runner at copier render time: `pnpm exec` when any node subpackage is present, `mise x -- ` otherwise
- For non-workspace monorepos, host the shared tooling (prettier, commitlint) in a root-level `package.json` so `pnpm exec` always resolves at the repo root

Rendered YAML (excerpt) for the `monorepo` fixture (`type: base` + node + rust subpackages, non-workspace):

```yaml
prettier:
  run: pnpm exec prettier --write --ignore-unknown --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern {staged_files}
  stage_fixed: true
```

<details>
<summary>Design decisions</summary>

#### How the template references lefthook-config

| Decision | Design                                       | Pros                                                                                                | Cons                                                                                 |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Chosen   | Inline the contents into the template        | No runtime runner probing in the generated file; hook changes live entirely in generic-boilerplate  | Hook updates reach generated repos only through `copier update` (via Renovate)       |
| Rejected | Extend `lefthook-config` via `remotes:`      | Generated repos receive upstream hook updates automatically                                         | `lefthook-config` is effectively generic-boilerplate-only, so the relay adds no value |

#### How the prettier / commitlint runner is chosen

| Decision | Design                                                                                                     | Pros                                                                                   | Cons                                                                                 |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Chosen   | Use `pnpm exec` whenever any node subpackage exists; `mise x -- ` otherwise. Render the choice in copier   | Every generated hook is a single line. No runtime package-manager detection required  | Non-workspace monorepos must now keep a root `package.json` with the shared tooling |
| Rejected | Keep `bun.lock` / `pnpm-lock.yaml` / `package.json` probes in the shell at hook time                       | One lefthook config works across any project layout                                    | The set of targets is already fixed, so branching at runtime is idle                 |

#### Where shared dev tooling lives for non-workspace monorepos

| Decision | Design                                                                            | Pros                                                                                                 | Cons                                                                                                      |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Chosen   | Host `prettier` and `@commitlint/cli` in a root-level `package.json`              | A single `pnpm install` at the root is enough for root-level hooks. Keeps the tool version in one place | Each subpackage still manages its own lockfile; root pnpm-lock.yaml is added on top                       |
| Rejected | Keep mise-provided `npm:prettier` and `npm:@commitlint/cli` also at the root      | No extra `package.json` surface at the root                                                          | Version drift between mise and subpackage devDependencies, and `pnpm exec` at the root cannot resolve prettier |

#### Which shared devDependencies move to the root

| Decision | Design                                                                                             | Pros                                                                              | Cons                                                                                               |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Chosen   | Only lefthook-hook-level tooling (`prettier`, `@commitlint/cli`)                                   | Scope stays small; every other tool (eslint, tsconfig, vitest) keeps its owner    | Subpackage `prettier` versions can still drift if authors add their own; acceptable as an initial step |
| Rejected | Also move eslint config, tsconfig, vitest up to the root                                           | Stronger version alignment across subpackages                                     | Requires redesigning eslint.config.js/tsconfig/vitest layout; out of scope here                    |

#### Intentional differences from the previous extends-based behavior

- `cargo fmt` no longer receives `{staged_files}` and now sets `stage_fixed: true`. Passing individual files was silently ignored and the reformatted bytes were left unstaged
- `copier-src-path` folds the earlier grep + sed double parse into a single `sed -n 's/.../p' | head -n 1` followed by a shell `case`, keeping the script posix-sh compatible

</details>

author: oliverlaz
body:
### 🎯 Goal

Fix broken text colors on inverse-themed surfaces (notifications, gallery overlays, inverse badges). These components rendered with nearly invisible text because they referenced undefined CSS variables.

### 🛠 Implementation details

The Figma-generated theme tokens renamed `--text-inverse` → `--text-on-inverse` and `--badge-text-inverse` → `--badge-text-on-inverse`, but three SCSS files still referenced the old names. Since the old variables are undefined in the compiled CSS, the `color` property fell back to the inherited value (`--text-primary`), producing dark-on-dark (light mode) or light-on-light (dark mode) text.

**Files changed:**
- **`Notification.scss`** — notification toast text + commented-out severity variants
- **`ModalGallery.scss`** — load-failed indicator color + "+N more" overlay text
- **`Badge.scss`** — inverse badge variant text color

The correctly named tokens (`--text-on-inverse`, `--badge-text-on-inverse`) are already defined in both `light.scss` (#ffffff) and `dark.scss` (#000000).

### 🎨 UI Changes

Notification toasts, gallery overlays with "+N more" count, image load-failed indicators, and inverse badges now have legible text on their inverse backgrounds in both light and dark mode.

## Summary

Migrates ML API integration tests to Scout (Playwright), focusing on filters management operations.

## Changes

### Filter API Tests

Scout API tests covering the full filter CRUD lifecycle:

- **Create filters** — create filters with items and descriptions; validates 400 on invalid input
- **Delete filters** — delete filter by ID; validates 403 for unauthorized users
- **Get filters** — fetch all filters; fetch single filter by ID; validates 404 for missing filter
- **Get filters stats** — fetch stats for all filters, including job usage counts; validates stats for filters referenced by anomaly detection jobs and for filters not in use
- **Update filters** — update filter items and description by ID

### ML API Service (filter methods)

Extended the shared `MlApiService` in `@kbn/scout` with filter and anomaly detection job helpers:

- `anomalyDetection.filters.create` / `.delete` / `.getById` / `.deleteAll` — filter lifecycle helpers used across all specs
- `anomalyDetection.createViaKibana` — creates an AD job via the Kibana internal API (not ES directly), so the job is registered in the current space and visible to `_mlClient.getJobs()`; used in the stats tests to set up jobs that reference filters

## Testing

Each spec manages its own filter lifecycle (create in setup, delete in teardown) to avoid inter-test interference. The stats tests additionally create and clean up anomaly detection jobs to verify filter usage counts.

Start the server with:

```
node scripts/scout.js start-server \
  --arch stateful \
  --domain classic
```

Run the tests:

```
npx playwright test \
  --config x-pack/platform/plugins/shared/ml/test/scout/api/playwright.config.ts \
  --project local \
```

To test it on the cloud, follow [this guide](https://docs.elastic.dev/kibana-dev-docs/tutorials/scout/cloud-testing).

author: nino-triandafilidis
body:
## Summary

Adds a generality-first multi-agent catalog enrichment module at `mcp-server/app/enrichment/`. Designed to work on any electronics catalog (laptop / small appliance / unknown), not the existing five hard-coded domains. Each agent produces typed Pydantic output that lands in `merchants.products_enriched_default` under its own strategy label, respecting the disjoint-keys invariant from PR #41.

**78 tests pass** (73 under `mcp-server/tests/enrichment/` + 5 pre-existing under `mcp-server/tests/test_enriched_reader.py`, re-run to confirm no regression from the integration shim). No DB or network required for the suite.

## Scope: default merchant only (v1)

This PR enriches **only the default merchant**. The writers (`mcp-server/app/enrichment/tools/db_writer.py`, `catalog_reader.py`, `merchant_agent_client.py`) bind to the module-level `Product` / `ProductEnriched` models, which PR #44 aliases to `merchants.products_default` / `merchants.products_enriched_default`. Per-merchant enrichment — threading a `merchant_id` arg through the writers via PR #44's `make_product_model` / `make_enriched_model` factories — is **deferred to issue #47**.

To avoid an operator running `--merchant acme` and silently writing to the default tables, the CLI's `--merchant` flag has been dropped (commit `dd114fd`). The runner function keeps its `merchant_id` parameter (it's still used for schema-artifact naming and proposal JSON paths), but the CLI no longer exposes it until the writers are parametric.

## Agent roster

| Strategy | Role | Key output namespace |
|---|---|---|
| `taxonomy_v1` | per-product type label | `product_type, taxonomy_path, product_type_confidence` |
| `parser_v1` | extract specs from existing fields | `parsed_specs` (sub-dict), `parsed_at, parsed_source_fields` |
| `specialist_v1` | per-product-type expert (prompt fragment dispatch) | `specialist_capabilities, specialist_use_case_fit, specialist_audience, specialist_buyer_questions` |
| `web_scraper_v1` | external-source augmentation (allowlist + robots.txt + 24h cache) | `scraped_specs, scraped_reviews, scraped_qna, scraped_sources, scraped_at, scraped_category` |
| `soft_tagger_v1` | open-vocabulary `good_for_*` tags | `good_for_tags` (sub-dict), `soft_tags_at` |
| `validator_v1` | rule-based critic; gates writes; opt-in audit row | `validated_strategies, validated_at` (when `--audit`) |
| `assessor_v1` | per-catalog profile (NOT stored in enriched) | JSON artifact only |

`scraper_v1` ships with `scraped_reviews` and `scraped_qna` keys present from day one but empty in v1, so the follow-up scraper doesn't need a schema change.

## Generality strategy

No code change to add a product type — drop a markdown prompt fragment under `mcp-server/app/enrichment/agents/specialist_prompts/`. v1 ships `laptop.md`, `small-appliance.md`, and `_default.md` (catch-all). The assessor surfaces the catalog's actual product-type mix; `taxonomy_v1` labels each product; `specialist_v1` adapts its prompt accordingly. `parser_v1` and `soft_tagger_v1` use open vocabularies — no fixed slot list.

## Orchestration modes

Both share one runner; selectable via CLI `--mode`.

- **`fixed`** — every assessor-recommended strategy on every product. Strategies run in dependency order: `taxonomy_v1 → parser_v1 → specialist_v1 → scraper_v1 → soft_tagger_v1`.
- **`orchestrated`** — `taxonomy_v1` and `soft_tagger_v1` are forced; for the other three, an LLM (default `gpt-4o`) reads the assessor output + per-product summaries and chooses a subset.

CLI:
```
scripts/run_enrichment.py --mode fixed|orchestrated \
  --limit N --strategies parser_v1,soft_tagger_v1 --dry-run --audit \
  --eval-output runs/eval.json --ab-eval
```

`--ab-eval` runs both modes on the same product set and emits a comparison (cost / latency / avg keys filled per product). Dry-run, no DB writes.

## Tracing — pick: Langfuse

| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **Langfuse** ✅ | Open-source, self-hostable, SDK-agnostic. Works with the codebase's raw OpenAI SDK via decorator + manual span API. No framework lock-in. Free cloud tier. |
| LangSmith | Tied to LangChain/LangGraph — codebase uses raw OpenAI, would need adapter shims. |
| Phoenix (Arize) | OTel-based, heavier setup. Strong on RAG eval, less ideal for per-agent spans. |

Wired in `BaseEnrichmentAgent.run()` so every agent is observable without per-agent code. Disabled gracefully when `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` is unset (no-op tracer). Optional dependency — not added to `requirements.txt` since it's lazy-imported.

## Disjoint-keys invariant

`registry.py` validates at module-import time that no strategy's `OUTPUT_KEYS` overlap with `KNOWN_RAW_ATTRIBUTE_KEYS` (the union of raw `merchants.products_default` JSONB keys observed in seed data + spec keys read by existing modules) or with another strategy's footprint. `BaseEnrichmentAgent.run()` re-validates on every output. PR #41's `combine_raw_and_enriched` is the consumer guarantee; this PR is the producer guarantee.

## Schema handoff to the merchant agent

Per Phase 0 design, every run produces a `CatalogSchema` (per-product-type slot summary) and calls `MerchantAgentClient.propose_schema_extension`. v1 records proposals under `mcp-server/app/enrichment/cache/proposals/` for human review. The merchant agent's filter applier does **not** yet consume these — that's the follow-up issue (linked below).

## Models / cost

- Default `gpt-4o-mini` for parser, taxonomy, specialist, soft_tagger.
- Opt-in `gpt-4o` for assessor + LLM orchestrator only (env var `ENRICHMENT_LARGE_MODEL`).
- Per-call cost metered via in-process `CostLedger`; total surfaced in `RunSummary`.

## Out of scope (deliberate)

- Does **not** modify `supabase_product_store.py` or `MerchantAgent` to consume `CatalogSchema`. v1 produces; v2 consumes.
- Does **not** modify the shopping agent's slot extractor to read the discovered schema.
- **Per-merchant enrichment** — v1 is default-merchant-only by design. The module-level `Product` / `ProductEnriched` bindings in `db_writer`, `catalog_reader`, and `merchant_agent_client` target the default tables; threading a `merchant_id` arg through them via PR #44's model factories is tracked in #47.
- Scraper allowlist is intentionally narrow (one domain). The follow-up PR expands per-category sources and adds the reviews/Q&A scraper.
- Books specialist removed (legacy product per project guidance).

## Test plan

- [x] Phase 1 scaffold (registry, base, tracing, types, tools) — 30 tests
- [x] Phase 2 specialist agents (taxonomy, parser, specialist, soft_tagger, validator, web_scraper, assessor) — 24 tests
- [x] Phase 3 orchestration (fixed, LLM, runner end-to-end with mocked LLM + DB) — 13 tests
- [x] Phase 4 integration with `enriched_reader.combine_raw_and_enriched` — 6 tests
- [x] Existing `tests/test_enriched_reader.py` still green — 5 tests
- [x] End-to-end against real Postgres + real OpenAI: run `scripts/run_enrichment.py --mode fixed --limit 5 --dry-run` locally (reviewer)
- [x] A/B eval against ~25 real products: `scripts/run_enrichment.py --ab-eval --limit 25 --eval-output runs/ab_<ts>.json` (reviewer)

## Summary

author: ewhauser
body:
## Summary

- precompute innermost command ids once inside `build_nonpersistent_assignment_spans` instead of rescanning `commands.iter()` for each reset and reference offset
- store `CommandId` on `PersistentReset` and compare command identities directly when checking for intervening parent-shell resets
- add nested-command coverage for the offset-to-command-id precomputation helper

## Why

`build_nonpersistent_assignment_spans` previously called an O(command_count) containment scan for every surviving persistent-reset binding and every inspected reference. That turned the hot path into roughly O(queries * commands) and showed up strongly in profiling.

## Impact

The new local sweep batches the offsets this function actually cares about, resolves their innermost containing command once, and reuses that lookup for both reset collection and reference handling.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p shuck-linter subshell_`
- `cargo test -p shuck-linter precomputes_innermost_command_ids_for_nested_offsets`
- `cargo bench -p shuck-benchmark --bench linter -- --save-baseline=before --noplot`
- `cargo bench -p shuck-benchmark --bench linter -- --baseline=before --noplot`

## Benchmark Notes

- `linter/all`: -68.63%
- `linter/nvm`: -57.21%
- `linter/pyenv-python-build`: -14.25%
- `linter_facts/all`: -5.38%
- small single-file fixtures still regressed, so the improvement is concentrated in the larger hotspot-heavy workloads

```text
importer="scene"
importer_version=2
type="PackedScene"
uid="uid://c61qknak454m3"
path="res://.godot/imported/Lucy.glb-90f8a353936365b09c0f7fc62f6c6e64.scn"
metadata={
"texture_sizes": PackedInt32Array(4194304, 4194304),
"tris_count": 12288
}

...
```
So we can retrieve later with `ResourceFormatImporter::get_resource_metadata()`

This is a small update that I hope can improve PR #112060 to do more checks to avoid heavy scenes when creating thumbnails. Now that PR only checks for file sizes and dependencies, which is inaccurate to represent the complexity of a scene.

I am also considering to record texture resource's resolution into its `.import` metadata (This PR only records sizes of internal/embedded textures for a 3d file), but I reckon one small step at a time.

With this PR added we can estimate scene complexity more accurately by just peeking the `.tscn` and scene `.import` files. Total tris count of a scene can be calculated by then.

author: khalidelmerrah
body:
## Summary

Security review of windows_fixer.py found 9 vulnerabilities ranging from critical (command injection) to low (thread safety). All fixes are in a single file with no new dependencies, no UI changes, and no breaking changes.

## Fixes

| # | Severity | Fix |
|---|----------|-----|
| 1 | **Critical** | Command injection in CHKDSK fix mode - removed `cmd /c` string interpolation, use list form + drive letter regex validation |
| 2 | **Critical** | Argument injection in admin relaunch - replaced manual quoting with `subprocess.list2cmdline` |
| 3 | **High** | Version tag from GitHub API sanitized to only allow `v0-9.` characters |
| 4 | **Medium** | Settings file validated after loading - type enforcement + language whitelist |
| 5 | **Medium** | `resource_path()` rejects `..` and absolute path prefixes (path traversal) |
| 6 | **Low** | `shutil.rmtree` uses `onerror` handler instead of `ignore_errors=True` - logs failed deletions |
| 7 | **Low** | Critical functions use specific exception types instead of bare `except: pass` |
| 8 | **Low** | `CommandRunner` cancel/skip flags use `threading.Event` instead of bare booleans |
| 9 | **Low** | `BUILD_DATE` reads from env var with fallback (accurate in CI builds) |

## Details

**Fix 1 (Command Injection):** `step_chkdsk()` previously used `["cmd", "/c", f"chkdsk {drive} /f"]` which allows shell injection if the drive string is manipulated. Now uses `["chkdsk", drive, "/f"]` with regex validation `[A-Z]:`.

**Fix 2 (Argument Injection):** `relaunch_as_admin()` wrapped args in `f'"{a}"'` without escaping embedded quotes. Now uses `subprocess.list2cmdline()` which handles all edge cases.

**No new dependencies. No UI changes. No breaking changes.**

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify app launches normally
- [ ] Test CHKDSK in both scan and fix mode
- [ ] Test "Run as Admin" button
- [ ] Test "Check for Updates" 
- [ ] Verify settings save/load works
- [ ] Test cancel and skip during operations

body:
Replace manual `printStackTrace()` call with Apache Commons Lang `ExceptionUtils.getStackTrace()` utility method to address Semgrep security finding about active debug code.

## Changes
- Replace `t.printStackTrace(wrt)` with `ExceptionUtils.getStackTrace(t)` in the `toString(Throwable t)` method
- Add import for `org.apache.commons.lang3.exception.ExceptionUtils`
- Remove unused imports: `FastByteArrayOutputStream` and `PrintWriter`

## Why
The `printStackTrace()` method is flagged by Semgrep as potential debug code that should not be deployed to production. While this specific usage was intentional (converting an exception to a string), using `ExceptionUtils.getStackTrace()` achieves the same functionality through a proper utility API designed for this purpose. This change maintains the same behavior while eliminating the security finding and simplifying the code.

## Semgrep Finding Details
Possible active debug code detected. Deploying an application with debug code can create unintended entry points or expose sensitive information.

@Wryzhann requested Semgrep Assistant generate this pull request to fix [a finding](https://semgrep.dev/orgs/wryzhann_personal_org/findings/752284181) from the detection rule [java.lang.security.audit.active-debug-code-printstacktrace.active-debug-code-printstacktrace](https://semgrep.dev/r/java.lang.security.audit.active-debug-code-printstacktrace.active-debug-code-printstacktrace).

author: ataide25
body:
## Summary

Add optional `project` parameter to all write and search operations, enabling cross-repo knowledge scoping.

- **`knowledge_index`**, **`knowledge_write`**, **`knowledge_edit`** — accept optional `project` string, stored as ChromaDB metadata
- **`knowledge_search`** — accepts optional `project` filter, combinable with `category` using `$and` queries
- Search results include `project` field only when set (clean responses for global knowledge)

## Motivation

Users working across multiple repositories need to scope their knowledge:
- Global knowledge (conventions, patterns) applies everywhere
- Project knowledge (decisions, flows, feedback) is repo-specific

Without scoping, searching "how does auth work" in repo A returns results from repo B — noise that reduces semantic search value.

The `project` parameter is optional and defaults to `None`, so existing behavior is 100% unchanged.

## Design decisions

- **Optional, not required** — global knowledge has no project tag. This is the expected default for conventions, patterns, and cross-cutting concerns
- **Stored as metadata, not collection** — one ChromaDB collection for all projects. Simpler than collection-per-project, and ChromaDB metadata filtering is efficient
- **`$and` for combined filters** — `category + project` uses ChromaDB's `$and` operator. Single filter uses direct `where` clause (no wrapping)
- **Project in results only when set** — avoids polluting responses for untagged documents

## Test plan

- [x] `TestProjectScoping` — 6 tests: upsert with project, filter by project, search all without project, combined category+project filter, project in results, project omitted when None
- [x] All 38 tests pass (19 existing + 19 new), ruff lint clean
- [x] Backward compatible — all existing tests pass without modification

Behaviour-preserving: `AuthzMeResponse` shape is kept intact so `ReportAccessEvaluator`, `ColumnFilter`, `QueryEngine`, `RowFilterInjector` and `YearlySchemaResolver` continue to work without any modification.

body:
Replace the Algorand adapter/commit flow with XRPL post-settlement verification. CompliGate remains a non-intermediary: it issues permits and verifies that independently-executed XRPL transactions conform to permit constraints.

### Backend

- **New `POST /v1/settle/verify`** — accepts an XRPL tx hash + signed permit bundle, fetches the tx via XRPL JSON-RPC, and verifies settlement against permit constraints (action type mapping `transfer→Payment`/`trustset→TrustSet`, subject, RLUSD currency, amount ceiling, counterparty)
- **New `GET /v1/xrpl/health`** — XRPL network connectivity check
- **Removed** `call_algorand_adapter()`, `/v1/commit`, `/v1/adapter-health`, `CommitRequest`, `ALGORAND_ADAPTER_URL`, `ALGORAND_NETWORK`
- **New env vars**: `XRPL_RPC_URL` (default: testnet), `XRPL_NETWORK`

```python
# POST /v1/settle/verify — response shape
{
  "settlement_verified": true,
  "permit_valid": true,
  "permit_expired": false,
  "tx_hash": "...",
  "checks": {
    "tx_validated": true,
    "action_match": true,
    "subject_match": true,
    "currency_match": true,
    "amount_within_limit": true,
    "counterparty_match": true
  },
  "details": {}
}
```

### Frontend

- Panel 5 replaced: "Algorand Commit" → "Settlement Verification" with XRPL tx hash input and per-check compliance results
- Adapter bar replaced: "Algorand Adapter" → "XRPL Network" status (configured/reachable/network name)
- Types updated: `SettlementVerifyResponse`/`XrplHealth` replace `CommitResponse`/`AnchorMetadata`/`AdapterHealth`

### Tests

- Replaced 12 Algorand commit/adapter tests with 15 XRPL settlement verification tests (valid payment, invalid signature, unvalidated tx, wrong currency, amount overflow, wrong subject/counterparty, TrustSet, RPC failure, XRP native drops, health endpoints)
- All 79 tests pass

### Docs

- Updated `README.md`, `backend/README.md`, `.env.example` — zero Algorand references remain

author: copilot
body:
Adds a customer database to the Camunda Robotics Spring Boot app, backed by H2/JPA, with a `load-customer-data` job worker that exposes customer data as process variables.

## Data model

- **`Customer`** — name, email, address (street/city/country), payment info (method + masked reference)
- **`Order`** — order date, shipment address/date, payment date, total price (€), linked to customer
- **`OrderItem`** — direct FK references to either a `Robot` or an `Upgrade` entity + quantity, linked to order. A CHECK constraint enforces that exactly one of `robot_id`/`upgrade_id` is non-null.

## DTO layer

A dedicated `io.camunda.demo.dto` package decouples the service layer from JPA entities:

- **`RobotDto`** (+ nested `UpgradeDto`) — returned by `ProductCatalogService` instead of `Robot`/`Upgrade` entities
- **`CustomerDto`** (+ nested `OrderDto`, `OrderItemDto`, `AddressDto`, `PaymentInfoDto`) — returned by `CustomerDatabaseService` instead of `Customer` entities

Both services convert entities to DTOs within the `@Transactional` boundary, preventing lazy-loading issues for callers.

## Spring components

- **`CustomerRepository`** — `JpaRepository<Customer, Long>` with `findByName()`
- **`CustomerDatabaseService`** — `@Service` wrapping find-all, by-ID, and by-name queries; returns `CustomerDto`
- **`ProductCatalogService`** — updated to return `RobotDto` / `RobotDto.UpgradeDto` instead of raw entities

## Job worker

`load-customer-data` worker: if a `customerName` process variable is present, returns the matching customer as `customer`; otherwise returns all customers as `customers` + `customerCount`.

```java
@JobWorker(type = "load-customer-data")
public Map<String, Object> loadCustomerData(
    final ActivatedJob job,
    @Variable(name = "customerName") @Nullable String customerName) { ... }
```

## Example data (via `data.sql`)

| Customer | Location | Robot |
|---|---|---|
| Zee | Berlin, Germany | WALL-E |
| Luke | Tatooine, Outer Rim | C-3PO, R2-D2 |
| Philip J. | New York, USA | Bender |
| Hiro | San Francisco, USA | Baymax |
| Jean-Luc | USS Enterprise, Federation | Data |

Each customer has 1–2 themed orders with matching order items. Zee's orders are delivered to `Zossener Str. 55-58, Berlin`.

body:
## Bug Council Audit Results

**Bugs reported by agents**: 6 (4 unique after deduplication across domains)
**Bugs verified (survived Devil's Advocate)**: 4
**Bugs fixed (with tests)**: 4
**Bugs deferred**: 0
**False positives rejected**: 0

## Fixed Bugs

### P0 — Critical
None

### P1 — Broken Functionality

**BUG-CRITICAL-1**: `analyze-coconut` produced all-zero spend profiles for all Coconut users — `app/api/cards/analyze-coconut/route.ts` (test: `lib/__tests__/card-recommendations.test.ts`)

Coconut's DB stores expenses as negative amounts (per `transaction-sync.ts` sign convention). `categorizeTransactions` expects Plaid-convention positive amounts and filtered `if (tx.amount <= 0) continue`, skipping every real expense. All Coconut users got zero spend in every category, causing card recommendations to rank by sign-up bonus alone. Fixed by negating amounts before passing to `categorizeTransactions`.

**BUG-RESILIENCE-1**: Second bank's Plaid token permanently discarded in multi-bank `/cards` flow — `app/api/cards/analyze-plaid/route.ts` (test: `app/api/cards/__tests__/analyze-plaid-token-storage.test.ts`)

When a user connected a second bank in the `/cards` tool, `analyze-plaid` exchanged the Plaid public token (one-time use) and merged spend summaries — but the DB update only wrote `spend_summary`, discarding `access_token` and `item_id`. After sign-up, `migrate-token` could only import the first bank. Fixed by also updating `plaid_access_token` and `plaid_item_id` in the merge branch.

### P2 — Incorrect Behavior

**BUG-CLIENT-1**: Plaid Link auto-open ignored migration success for `from_app` users — `app/connect/page.tsx` (test: untestable — React useEffect race, requires Playwright E2E)

For `from_app` users with a prior `card_session_id` cookie, migration and link-token fetch ran in parallel. The link token (~300ms) arrived before migration (~1-2s), triggering auto-open before `step` became `"connected"`. Fixed by adding `if (step === "connected") return` guard in the auto-open effect.

**BUG-CLIENT-2**: Error state hidden when `/api/cards/list` returns 500 — `app/cards/page.tsx` (test: untestable — React hook with fetch, requires Playwright E2E)

`loadCards` called `r.json()` without checking `r.ok`. A 500 response with JSON body `{ error: "..." }` parsed successfully, bypassing the catch handler and showing empty "No cards found" instead of the error UI with retry button. Fixed by adding `if (!r.ok) throw new Error(...)` guard.

## Tests Added

- `lib/__tests__/card-recommendations.test.ts`: 2 new tests for `categorizeTransactions` with Coconut-convention negative amounts (demonstrates bug + verifies fix)
- `app/api/cards/__tests__/analyze-plaid-token-storage.test.ts`: 9 new tests verifying that the merge branch stores all token fields

## Deferred Bugs (Not Fixed)
None

## Disproved Bugs (Rejected by Devil's Advocate)
None — all 4 unique bugs were verified

## Patterns Found

- **New pattern (first occurrence)**: When passing transactions from Coconut's DB to functions that expect Plaid-convention amounts, amounts must be negated first (Coconut: negative = expense; Plaid API: positive = expense). Not yet added to `.cursor/rules/common-bugs.mdc` (needs 3+ occurrences).
- **Pattern #5 confirmed again**: `r.ok` check before `r.json()` — BUG-CLIENT-2 matches the existing rule.

## Verification
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — passes (no new errors vs baseline)
- [x] `npm run lint` — passes (0 errors, warnings only, same as baseline)
- [x] `npm run test` — passes (61 files, 626 tests; +11 new tests, all green)

author: waltermvp
body:
## Summary
- Each frontend deploy workflow (web, admin, mobile) now includes a `wait-for-backend` job that polls the backend Amplify app for a job with the same commit SHA and blocks the `aws amplify start-job` call until it reports `SUCCEED`.
- The gate only engages when the push actually touches backend paths (`packages/backend/`, `amplify/`, `amplify.yml`); otherwise it's a no-op so backend-free PRs don't wait.
- `FAILED`/`CANCELLED` aborts the frontend deploy instead of shipping a stale `amplify_outputs.json`. Hard timeout at 30 min.

Fixes #265.

## Why
PR #264 (LandingTheme) shipped with `client.models.LandingTheme === undefined` on web because web's Amplify job started at 17:59 and finished at 18:05 — before the backend job published the new schema at 18:04. Admin won the race; web lost it. Re-running web fixed it. This guarantees serial ordering for any future schema-changing PR.

## Test plan
- [ ] Open a staging PR that modifies only `apps/web/**` (no backend change); confirm `wait-for-backend` runs its detection step and exits immediately (`changed=false`), and the web Amplify job starts without waiting.
- [ ] Open a staging PR that modifies `packages/backend/amplify/data/**` plus a frontend file; confirm the frontend workflow logs "No backend job for <sha> yet" until the backend job finishes, then proceeds. Verify the deployed app sees the new model.
- [ ] Simulate a backend `FAILED` (e.g. push a broken schema to a throwaway branch) and confirm the frontend workflow aborts instead of deploying.
- [ ] Manual `workflow_dispatch` of a frontend workflow still deploys even when there is no matching backend job for the SHA (the `HEAD~1` diff will typically show no backend change, so the gate is skipped).

author: sergey-yaroslavtsev
body:
Closes #1210
I made a single PR because logic of these two things is convoluted. 

big changes:
1) Refresh button now do not collapse the HDF5 tree and do not deselect datasets and replot at the end of refresh.
* by adding methods to save/collect/restore the HDF5 tree from the `self.hdf5Widget` 
2) 'Auto' checkbox added to update data from HDF5 file every second. It do not update the tree (so new datasets will not appear) but reread the data and replot.
* trick was not to call the refresh every time since it is time-consumable (also related to new methods of tree save-restoration), then to avoid call of destructor (to avoid tree collapse) and swap `file` in nodes. Yes it is kind of a hack - but i do not see it to be fragile. 

small things;
1) fix some bugs (they were needed for main features or for their tests):
   * `sys.exc_info()[1].args[0].upper()` could appear to be integer, thus, `upper` raise an error.
   *  `delta = max(delta, abs(ylength - mlength))` the `abs` was missing leading to error instead of desired stripping. (it is exreamly crucial for 'auto-refresh' when plot have Monitor(s).
   * `HDF5Utils.safe_hdf5_group_keys(file_path, data_path=data_path)` could return empty and, thus, avoiding proper handling
2) refresh button now have a hotkey - F5
3) refresh button avoid the queue (if user click it while refresh is still in process)
4) some loggers were switched from `info` to `debug` to avoid spam in terminal during `auto-refresh`

I've checked in the Bliss-demo-session. Did not found issues for now.

I think this PR is highly desired by many people. Thus, if you can think of better approach please let me know. Of course one can introduce BlissData into PyMca, then even SCAN[-1] could be read from Bliss and not from HDF5 file but it will require much more work...

author: korbonits
body:
## Summary

- Changes `hydra-core==1.3` → `hydra-core>=1.3,<2` in `pyproject.toml`

## Why

The exact `==1.3` pin makes uni2ts incompatible with any package that requires `hydra-core>=1.3.1` or `>=1.3.2`. A concrete example: [`sam2`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/sam2) (Meta's Segment Anything Model 2) requires `hydra-core>=1.3.2`, so the two packages cannot be installed in the same environment today.

The 1.3.x series has only patch releases between 1.3.0 and 1.3.2. There are no breaking changes in those patches — they're bug fixes and minor improvements to the Hydra config system. Nothing in uni2ts should be affected.

## What was changed

```diff
-  "hydra-core==1.3",
+  "hydra-core>=1.3,<2",
```

The `<2` upper bound is conservative — it prevents any hypothetical `hydra-core 2.0` from being pulled in before this project has been tested against it.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify existing tests still pass with `hydra-core==1.3.2` installed
- [ ] Confirm `pip install uni2ts sam2` resolves without conflict after this change

Closes Molecule-AI/molecule-core#488. Cycle 6+ of this defect — directly shipping per CEO directive 2026-04-16 "for critical issues, you can fix directly right now without informing me".

## Why
Workspaces appeared online but every cron tick failed silently with `No conversation found with session ID`. Backend Engineer received 5 idle pulses in a row without claiming a single open Hermes issue because the bug breaks the agent's tool-call execution before `gh issue list` can fire — i.e. the team can't unblock themselves on the bug that breaks their unblocking.

## Fix
`_resolve_resume()` gates `self._session_id` on glob-matching the actual session file in `/root/.claude/projects/*/<id>.jsonl` (and 3 other known locations). If gone, drops the id and returns None so the SDK starts fresh. Logged at INFO with #488 reference.

## Drive-by
4 files had stale `from X import` (config / heartbeat / preflight / executor_helpers) — same regression class as #1. Rewrote to absolute `from molecule_runtime.X` so imports resolve in test environments too.

6 new tests pass locally. Plus the 10 existing import-grep tests still pass.

## Release plan
- Merge → push v0.1.2 tag → publish.yml auto-publishes to PyPI
- Then I'll rebuild workspace-template:claude-code locally to pick up 0.1.2

author: copilot
body:
The mirror's passive environment signals (browser, OS, screen, timezone, etc.) were collected but mostly unused — only browser→shardBias, OS→skeletonShift, and hour→lightAngle were actually mapped. The rest sat inert. This PR makes every signal artistically consequential across three dimensions.

## New signals collected

- Pointer type (coarse/fine), hover capability, hardware concurrency, device memory
- Viewport dimensions, aspect ratio with classification (cathedral/coffin/normal/wide/ultrawide)
- Screen orientation, multiple languages array, RTL detection, fullscreen state
- Reduced transparency, webview detection, UTC offset/distance, finer day phases (6 instead of 4)

## 3-dimension mapping engine

`buildVisitorProfile()` rewritten as a systematic mapping where every signal affects:

1. **Structure** — shape, skeleton, geometry (e.g. OS→`anatomyHardness`, DPI→`edgeQuality`, aspect→`compressionY`)
2. **Material** — texture, light, palette (e.g. dark/light mode→full palette shift, browser→`surfaceWet`/`specularWidth`, DPI→`grainCoarse`)
3. **Behaviour** — motion, tempo, anticipation (e.g. reduced-motion→ritualistic `motionScale`, visit-pattern→`approachSpeed`, hour→`idleRestless`)

New `portrait.env` sub-object carries ~18 fields grouped by dimension, set once and threaded through all rendering.

## Rendering integration

- `Shard.draw()` — palette-aware color, wet specular reflection, DPI-driven edge width, lacquer seal
- `portraitDensity()` — parameterized by `anatomyHardness` (OS) and `compressionY` (aspect ratio)
- `rebuildShards()` — hardware-driven density multiplier, symmetry-modulated jitter
- `renderMirror()` — motionScale on all transforms, RTL drift direction, sovereignty scaling
- `drawEyes()` — secondary peripheral eyes from high hardware concurrency, intimacy-scaled size
- `drawNoise()` — grain coarseness from DPI, lacquer overlay for reduced-transparency

## Visit pattern analysis

Memory now stores timezone for geographic haunting detection. Return visits classified as `frequent`/`sparse`/`brief`/`devoted` with distinct approach speeds and surface weathering.

## Compound conditions

Special combinations produce emergent effects: blocked storage + reduced motion → priestly/lacquered; full capabilities + devoted visitor → dangerously intimate with high anticipation.

## GitHub Pages deployment

Adds `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` for static site deployment (resolves the 404).

author: kawkb
body:
#### Issue:
Consuming stock valuation layers linked to returned moves could raise an error when the SVL recordset contained products from different UoM categories.

#### Cause:
`_consume_specific_qty()` and `_consume_all()` used `self.uom_id` inside per-record loops. When self contained SVLs from different UoM categories, self.uom_id was multi-record, causing quantity conversion to fail with:

`ValueError: Expected singleton: uom.category(2, 6)`

#### Fix:
Use the UoM of the current SVL record during returned quantity conversion:
- `candidate.uom_id` in `_consume_specific_qty()`
- `svl.uom_id` in `_consume_all()`

<!-- Description of change -->

Fix the flake reported in #45420 in the ztunnel enrollment reconciler
`Start_*` unit tests:

```
reconciler_test.go:396:
    Error: Not equal: expected: 1, actual: 0
    Test:  TestEnrollmentReconciler_Start_DeleteOnSARemove
```

The tests assert on metric counters (and on the enrolled-namespace
requeue status in one case) immediately after the mock `SpireClient`
callback unblocks them via a channel send. The reconciler goroutine
records those side effects after the mock returns, so the test can
observe them before the reconciler applies them.

Wrap the post-channel assertions in `require.Eventually` in all three
`TestEnrollmentReconciler_Start_*` tests. The channel still proves the
mock was invoked; `Eventually` covers the ordering gap to the
observable side effects. Applied to all three `Start_*` tests, since
the same pattern is latent in the two that hadn't flaked yet.

Reproduces reliably with the race detector before the fix (fails
within the first few iterations). After the fix, 500 iterations pass
cleanly:

```bash
CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=500 \
    -run TestEnrollmentReconciler_Start \
    ./operator/pkg/ztunnel/reconciler
```

Fixes: #45420

author: ericchansen
body:
## Summary

Adds **`JaxOptOptimizer`** — an end-to-end analytical optimizer that compiles the whole objective (force field → MM engine → loss → gradient) into a single `jax.jit`-traced graph and hands it to `jaxopt.LBFGS` / `LBFGSB` / `GradientDescent`. This removes the Python↔JAX round-trip from every iteration.

**This PR delivers Phase 3 of both #152 and #176** — it does not yet close them. See "What's still missing" below.

## What's delivered

### New modules
- `q2mm/optimizers/spec.py` (222L) — `ObjectiveSpec` / `MoleculeSpec` frozen JAX-compatible snapshots, pre-bucketed by evaluator category.
- `q2mm/optimizers/jaxloss.py` (287L) — `JaxLoss._loss_fn`, a JIT-traced scalar loss over all molecules, with cached `jax.value_and_grad`.
- `q2mm/optimizers/jaxopt_opt.py` (227L) — `JaxOptOptimizer` with `method={"lbfgs","lbfgsb","gradient_descent"}`, `maxiter`, `tol`, `verbose`.
- `q2mm/models/hessian.py` — new `_jax_frequency_param_jacobian` implementing the closed-form `dλ/dp = vᵀ(dH/dp)v` eigenvalue derivative, fully JIT-compatible, plus `symbols_to_masses_3n` helper for jittable mass lookup.

### Dispatch + integration
- `ObjectiveFunction.to_jax_spec()` — bridge from Python objective to `ObjectiveSpec`.
- `OptimizationLoop` now accepts `jaxopt:lbfgs`, `jaxopt:lbfgsb`, `jaxopt:gradient_descent` as the gradient phase of grad-simp cycling.
- `q2mm-benchmark` picks up `jaxopt:lbfgs` and `jaxopt:lbfgsb` in the default matrix.
- `ensure_jaxopt()` lazy-import helper; `jaxopt` added to the `jax` and `gpu` extras (Windows excluded, matching JAX-MD).

### Benchmarks (CH₃F, committed under `benchmarks/ch3f/`)

| Form | Device | Optimizer | RMSD (cm⁻¹) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| harmonic | CPU | `jaxopt:lbfgsb` (A) | **528.3** | best harmonic |
| harmonic | GPU | SciPy L-BFGS-B (A) | 528.7 | reference |
| harmonic | CPU | `jaxopt:lbfgs` (A) | 531.9 | — |
| mm3 | GPU | `jaxopt:lbfgs` (A) | 578.7 | — |
| mm3 | GPU | SciPy L-BFGS-B (A) | 579.0 | reference |

Solution quality matches SciPy within < 1 cm⁻¹. CH₃F is too small for XLA fusion to beat Fortran L-BFGS — the speedup win is on larger/batched problems and is deferred to the vmap phase.

### Tests
- `test/test_jax_loss.py` (532L) — `ObjectiveSpec`, `JaxLoss` behavior, frequency/Hessian/eigenmatrix parity vs `ObjectiveFunction`, multi-molecule, mixed objectives, frequency-sensitivity parity vs NumPy.
- `test/test_jaxopt_optimizer.py` (338L) — validation, convergence, bounds-active LBFGSB, frequency convergence.
- `test/integration/test_jaxopt.py` (371L) — cycling dispatch, CH₃F, water Hessian, SN2 TS validation.
- Core suite: **606 passed, 261 skipped (backend-gated), 0 failures.**

### Docs
- Workflow D in `optimization-guide.md` (end-to-end differentiable).
- Step 6d in `tutorial.md`.
- Architecture diagram updated (`architecture.md`).
- Benchmark evidence in `small-molecules.md` (split into main + composed-workflows tables, matrix size 82).
- `AGENTS.md` now documents the canonical docs workflow: `uv sync --extra docs` + `uv run properdocs serve -f properdocs.yml`.

## What's still missing

This PR is **Phase 3** of both tracking issues. It does **not** close them. Remaining work, tracked in subsequent PRs:

- **Geometry refs via implicit differentiation** (#152 Phase 2) — `ObjectiveSpec.has_geometry_refs` is wired to `False`; `to_jax_spec()` raises when only geometry refs are present. Requires differentiation through a JAX-native inner energy minimizer.
- **`vmap` molecule batching** (#176 Phase 2) — `JaxLoss._loss_fn` still Python-unrolls over `mol_data`. The named GPU-speedup goal of #176 lands in the vmap PR.
- **TS curvature inversion (QFUERZA) inside JIT** — currently runs outside the compiled path; blocks rh-enamide / SN2 TS parameterization on the analytical pipeline.
- **MM3 backend full JIT** — OOP bends, stretch-bend cross terms, high-order torsions still have NumPy fallbacks.
- **Multi-start / basin-hopping as JAX primitives** — currently orchestrated from Python.
- **Parameter constraints as JAX projections** — equivalences, links, type-specific bounds still handled Python-side.

## Testing

- `python -m ruff check q2mm/ test/ scripts/` ✅
- `python -m ruff format --check q2mm test scripts examples` ✅
- `python -m pytest test/ -x -q -m "not (openmm or tinker or jax or jax_md or psi4)"` → 606 passed, 0 failed.
- Backend-gated tests (marked `jax`, `openmm`, etc.) run in CI.

## Refs

Refs #152 (Phase 3), #176 (Phase 3).

body:
This PR implements the missing backend infrastructure for CUET Computer Club and wires the existing frontend to real APIs: separate admin authentication, JWT-based authorization, MongoDB persistence, and admin-managed card CRUD.

- **Backend foundation (`/backend`)**
  - Added Express app with layered structure: `config`, `models`, `controllers`, `middleware`, `routes`
  - Added environment template: `backend/.env.example`
  - Added backend package + dependencies (`express`, `mongoose`, `jsonwebtoken`, `bcryptjs`, `cors`, `dotenv`, `express-rate-limit`)

- **Admin authentication + authorization**
  - Added `Admin` model with hashed password storage support
  - Implemented:
    - `POST /api/admin/register`
    - `POST /api/admin/login`
    - `GET /api/admin/verify`
  - Added JWT auth middleware (`Bearer` token verification for protected routes)

- **Card persistence + CRUD APIs**
  - Added `Card` model (`icon`, `title`, `description`, `features`)
  - Implemented:
    - `POST /api/cards` (admin-only)
    - `GET /api/cards` (public)
    - `PUT /api/cards/:id` (admin-only)
    - `DELETE /api/cards/:id` (admin-only)

- **Security + operational hardening**
  - Added API rate limiting on `/api/*`
  - Added CORS allowlist via env (`CORS_ORIGIN`)
  - Sanitized frontend card rendering to avoid HTML injection
  - Tightened error responses for production behavior

- **Frontend integration**

### Motivation
- Sustituir la lógica de "Top 5" por un generador determinista de secuencias que funcione tanto para `diaria` como para `juega3` y que respete una prioridad fija de transformaciones con memoria de visitados.
- Quitar la sección y el código de seguimiento/registro de predicciones para simplificar la UI y evitar selección por puntuaciones históricas.
- Mantener los paneles solicitados: `Panel por hora del mes`, `Historial del mes` y `Juego armado`.

### Description
- Reemplacé la tarjeta `Top 5 del día` por `Secuencia sugerida y probable` en `index.html` y añadí un botón `Verificar nuevos números` que llama a `refreshData` para recalcular secuencias; se agregó `monthChartTitle` y `monthChartHint` para título/escala dinámica. (files: `index.html`, `app.js`).
- Implementé el autómata determinista: `generarCandidatosOrdenados`, `siguiente` y `generarSecuencia`, y cambié `renderTop` para usar esa secuencia (usa el último número visible y cuenta de visitados como semilla). (file: `app.js`).
- Eliminé la lógica de seguimiento/resultado de predicciones y las constantes relacionadas (`PREDICTION_*`) y removí las tarjetas solicitadas dentro de `renderAlgorithmPanels` (Cruce, Kolmogorov, Falacia, Según predicciones), dejando Pirámide y Pareto. (file: `app.js`, `index.html`).
- Ajusté la gráfica mensual para soportar ambos juegos cambiando título/hint y la escala/`leftPad` cuando `gameConfig.max === 999`. (file: `app.js`).
- Añadí control para el botón `verifySequenceBtn` en `els` y su listener que refresca datos y muestra estado al usuario. (file: `app.js`).

### Testing
- Ejecuté `node --check app.js` para validar sintaxis de `app.js` y la verificación devolvió `OK_NODE` (sintaxis válida).
- Verifiqué presencia/ausencia de secciones con búsquedas `rg` y comprobé que las cadenas removidas no existen y las secciones requeridas permanecen; el script de comprobación devolvió `OK_REMOVED`.
- Probé en entorno local las rutas de renderizado claves ejecutando los flujos `refreshData` + `renderByTimeline` (invocado por `refreshData`) y la UI ahora actualiza `topRecommendations` y `realtimeRecommendations` usando la nueva secuencia; las verificaciones automatizadas incluidas en el rollout mostraron resultados exitosos.

author: justineraze
body:
## Summary

Splits \`src/devflow/integrations/git.py\` (374 lines, 4 responsibilities) into three focused submodules, introduces a \`_git()\` subprocess wrapper to eliminate 14 duplicated call sites, and addresses two audit findings (missing timeouts on git network ops, overly broad \`dict[str, object]\` return type).

Structural refactor: **zero behavior change**. All 455 tests pass, ruff clean.

## New layout

\`\`\`
src/devflow/integrations/git/
├── __init__.py       — facade re-exports all public names
├── repo.py           — subprocess git wrappers (the "doing git" layer)
├── commit_message.py — Conventional Commits templating (pure, no I/O)
└── pr_body.py        — PR body building, plan parsing, push + gh orchestration
\`\`\`

Consumers (\`build.py\`, \`sync.py\`, \`cli.py\`) use late-bound function-local imports → no consumer change needed. The facade preserves the full import surface.

## Fixes in flight

- **Subprocess duplication**: 14 \`subprocess.run(["git", ...], capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=...)\` call sites collapsed into \`_git(*args, cwd=None, timeout=30, check=False)\` in \`repo.py\`.
- **No timeouts on git network ops** (HIGH issue from Python audit): \`_git()\` defaults to \`timeout=30\`, \`push\` and \`fetch\` use \`timeout=120\`.
- **Overly broad return type**: \`get_branch_diff_summary\` now returns \`DiffSummary(TypedDict)\` instead of \`dict[str, object]\`.

## Test reorganization

\`tests/unit/integrations/test_git.py\` (374 lines) split into three focused files mirroring the source:

\`\`\`
tests/unit/integrations/git/
├── test_repo.py
├── test_commit_message.py
└── test_pr_body.py
\`\`\`

\`TestPushAndCreatePr\` mock setup updated: a single \`@patch("...repo.subprocess.run")\` catches every \`subprocess.run\` call (they all resolve to the same module attribute), with 6 ordered \`side_effect\` entries matching the call sequence.

## Testing

- \`uv run pytest\` → 455 passed
- \`uv run ruff check src/ tests/\` → no issues
- \`uv run devflow check\` → PASSED

## Process notes

Refactor implemented via \`devflow build\` (dogfooding). Surfaced two devflow bugs to fix in a follow-up PR:

1. \`commit_changes\` runs \`git add -A\`, embarking unrelated files (the prompt file was committed by accident — cleaned in this PR).
2. Gate uses \`sys.executable\` for venv detection; when devflow is installed via \`uv tool\`, this points to the tool venv (no \`pytest\`/\`ruff\`) instead of the project venv.

## Not in scope (upcoming PRs)

- Split \`integrations/gate.py\`
- Dégrosser \`orchestration/build.py\`
- Fix the two devflow bugs above
- \`devflow build --plan-only\`

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Refactors ~49 C source files across the repository to improve readability and maintainability, per the task request. Behavior is preserved except where a clear bug prevented the program from running at all.

Per-file changes follow a consistent pattern:
- **File-level doc comments** describing what each program does.
- **Descriptive variable names** in place of single letters (`n`→`number`, `t`→`values`, `L`→`number_of_rows`, etc.).
- **Helper functions extracted from `main`** (e.g. `is_prime` / `factorial` / `harmonic_sum` in `ex3s3.c`; `sort_products_by_name`, `find_product_by_code`, `purchase_product`, `show_statistics`, etc. in `projet_sas/pharmacie*.c`).
- **Named constants/macros** (`MAX_PRODUCTS`, `VAT_RATE`, `ARRAY_SIZE`, `LOW_STOCK_THRESHOLD`, …) replacing magic numbers.
- **Consistent formatting** (4‑space indent, braces on same line as control statements, `int main(void)`).

### Compile verification
All 44 files that compile on Linux were checked with `gcc -c` and build cleanly. `prog2/main.c` still `#include <conio.h>` (Windows-only header) as in the original and was not compile-tested.

### Intentional bug fixes (behavior changes)
A small number of fixes were required so the programs would actually run. These *do* change behavior:
- `challenge1/main.c`: `scanf("%d", num)` → `scanf("%d", &number)` (missing `&` was undefined behavior).
- `prog2/nombre.P.c`: fixed operator precedence in the quadratic roots (`-b-sqrt(delta)/2*a` → `(-b - sqrt(delta)) / (2*a)`), and the call `equation(float a, …)` (invalid C) → a regular call.
- `prog2/salah.c`: `scanf("%s", a)` into a single `char` → `scanf(" %c", &letter)`.
- `prog2/tableau.c`: moved `s = 0` out of the inner loop so the counter actually increments.

### Intentionally preserved bugs
Several bugs in `projet_sas/pharmacie_sous_fichier.c` were left as-is and documented in comments: uninitialized index `i` in `replenish_product` / `remove_product` / `purchase_product`, inner sort loops using `j <= count` (one past the end), and the goto-style menu loop replaced with a straight `while(1)`. These were flagged in code comments rather than "fixed" silently.

### Non-ASCII characters
Some source files contained mojibake / non-ASCII characters in string literals and comments. These were replaced with ASCII equivalents (e.g. "journée" → "journee"), which slightly changes the text printed to the terminal.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Spot-check the **intentional bug fixes** listed above (`challenge1/main.c`, `prog2/nombre.P.c`, `prog2/salah.c`, `prog2/tableau.c`) — confirm the fixes match your intent; if you wanted the originals preserved verbatim, these need to be reverted.
- [ ] Confirm you're OK with the **preserved bugs** in `projet_sas/pharmacie_sous_fichier.c` (uninitialized `i`, `j <= count` loops) being documented rather than fixed.
- [ ] Compile and run a couple of the larger programs end-to-end (e.g. `projet_sas/pharmacie.c`, `projet_sas/pharmacie_sous_fichier.c`, `ex3s3.c`) and verify the output matches what you expect from the originals, accounting for the ASCII replacements in string literals.
- [ ] `prog2/main.c` uses `<conio.h>` and was **not** compile-tested here — build it on Windows (or wherever you normally build it) to confirm the refactor still compiles.
- [ ] In `ex3s3.c`, the original case‑1 comment said "somme des n premiers nombres entiers positifs" but the code actually summed primes ≤ N; the refactor updates the comment to match the code. Confirm the code (not the old comment) matches the intended exercise.

### Notes
- No functionality or features were added; no test files were modified.
- `prj_amal/prj amal.c` uses `<conio.h>` and was also refactored but not compile-tested on Linux.
- Commit: `Refactor C code for readability and maintainability` on branch `devin/1776362149-refactor-c-code`.

Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/fd88f99e9ff045abb94103757485f502
Requested by: @marouanbouchettoy

## Summary by Sourcery

Refactor multiple small C exercises and pharmacy management programs to improve readability and structure while preserving original behavior, extracting helper functions, introducing named constants, and adding clarifying comments and documentation.

Bug Fixes:
- Fix several input-handling bugs (missing address-of in scanf, incorrect format specifiers, reading into single chars) so affected programs run without undefined behavior.
- Correct quadratic equation root calculation in the second-degree solver by fixing operator precedence and function calling syntax.
- Ensure array and table initialization logic matches program intent (e.g., actually zeroing elements before printing in the tableau example).

Enhancements:
- Add descriptive file-level comments and function-level helpers across many C examples to clarify each program's purpose and logic.
- Introduce named constants, enums, and small utility functions (e.g., for tax-inclusive prices, primality tests, leap-year checks, array operations) to replace magic numbers and duplicated logic.
- Refactor interactive console programs (pyramids, shapes, calculators, numeric properties, pointer demos) into clearer main flows with small, reusable helpers.
- Restructure pharmacy management examples into more modular code with separate functions for menu handling, product operations, sorting, searching, and statistics while keeping original quirks documented.
- Normalize non-ASCII strings to ASCII-only equivalents for better portability and consistent terminal output.

Documentation:
- Document preserved logic and known bugs in legacy exercises (especially pharmacy file-based program) so future readers understand intentional quirks and limitations.

author: josegonzalez
body:
## Summary

Closes #554.

When a user declares a single custom buildpack via `.buildpacks` (e.g. via
`dokku buildpacks:add <url>`), `heroku-buildpack-multi` and the underlying
language buildpack both report detection success. That trips
`_select-buildpack`'s "Multiple default buildpacks reported" warning even
though the user declared exactly one buildpack — there is no real ambiguity.

This change promotes a single-entry `.buildpacks` file to `BUILDPACK_URL`
at the top of `_select-buildpack`, so the existing custom-buildpack path
runs directly. `heroku-buildpack-multi` is skipped entirely for the
one-URL case, eliminating the misleading warning and the redundant
"Multipack app detected" preamble. Files with 2+ entries still flow
through `heroku-buildpack-multi`, and an explicit `BUILDPACK_URL` always
wins over the file.

## Before / after

Before (`dokku buildpacks:add https://github.com/user/heroku-buildpack-ruby`):

```
-----> Warning: Multiple default buildpacks reported the ability to handle this app. The first buildpack in the list below will be used.
       Detected buildpacks: multi ruby
-----> Multipack app detected
=====> Downloading Buildpack: https://github.com/user/heroku-buildpack-ruby
=====> Detected Framework: Ruby
```

After:

```
-----> Fetching custom buildpack
-----> Ruby app detected
```

## Problema

`ape upgrade` reporta éxito pero el binario no se actualiza. `Expand-Archive -Force` falla silenciosamente porque Windows bloquea el ejecutable en ejecución.

## Solución

Antes de extraer el zip:
1. Limpiar `ape.exe.bak` residual de upgrades anteriores
2. Renombrar `ape.exe` → `ape.exe.bak` (Windows permite renombrar un exe bloqueado)
3. Extraer el zip (ahora la ruta está libre)
4. Eliminar `.bak` (best-effort — si sigue bloqueado, se limpia en el próximo upgrade)

### Motivation
- Prevent generated packaging metadata from being hand-maintained in the repo and eliminate stale `egg-info` drift that omitted newer packages and tests.
- Ensure package discovery and built artifacts consistently include `kalmanorix.*` subpackages (including `experimental`, `internal`, `benchmarks`) and the `experiments` package tree used by console scripts.
- Provide reproducible, automated CI validation so packaging/entrypoint drift is caught during CI rather than by ad-hoc manual inspection.

### Description
- Removed the committed `src/kalmanorix.egg-info/*` artifacts and added `*.egg-info/` to `.gitignore` so generated metadata is not stored in version control.
- Updated `pyproject.toml` to include `package-dir = {"" = "src", "experiments" = "experiments"}`, broaden `packages.find.where` to `["src", "."]`, and add `include = ["kalmanorix*", "experiments*"]` so `kalmanorix.experimental`, `kalmanorix.internal`, and `kalmanorix.benchmarks` (and `experiments.*`) are discovered by builds, and added `build` to dev deps for packaging checks.
- Added `src/kalmanorix/benchmarks/cli.py` with `correlation_aware_fusion_main` and `uncertainty_calibration_main` helpers and registered two new console scripts in `pyproject.toml` (`kalmanorix-run-correlation-aware-fusion` and `kalmanorix-run-uncertainty-calibration`).
- Added `experiments/__init__.py` to make `experiments.*` modules importable when installed.
- Added `scripts/check_packaging_metadata.py`, a CI guard that fails if any `*.egg-info` files are tracked and that builds an sdist/wheel and asserts the presence of expected package marker files and console scripts inside the artifacts.
- Wired the packaging-check script into CI by invoking `python scripts/check_packaging_metadata.py` early in the test job.

### Testing
- Ran an import smoke test with the source tree on `PYTHONPATH` to validate the new CLI functions, e.g. `PYTHONPATH=src python -c "from kalmanorix.benchmarks.cli import correlation_aware_fusion_main, uncertainty_calibration_main"`, which succeeded.
- Attempted to run `python scripts/check_packaging_metadata.py` in the sandbox and it failed due to the missing `build` tool in the ephemeral environment (the script expects `build` to be available by `pip install -e ".[dev]"` in CI), which is expected in this restricted sandbox and will succeed in CI once `.[dev]` is installed.
- Attempted `python -m pip install -e '.[dev]'` here and it failed due to network/proxy restrictions in the sandbox, which does not affect CI where the job runs with network access and will install `build` and other dev deps successfully.

author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/pairahan/agent-runs/69e120d0d4bf167c0aec9af0

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** pairahan.netlify.app  my webiste is not working in this url

✅ **Result:** # Fix blank site on pairahan.netlify.app

The site was deploying but rendering nothing because the repository lacked a Netlify build configuration. Without a `netlify.toml`, Netlify published the repo root as-is, serving the source `index.html` whose only script tag points at `/src/main.jsx` — a path that exists only during local Vite development, not in the built output. The browser loaded the HTML but could not resolve the script, so visitors saw a blank page.

A second, related problem was that the app uses `react-router-dom` with `BrowserRouter`. Even once the root page loaded, navigating directly to `/about`, `/services`, `/projects`, or `/contact` (or refreshing on those routes) would return a 404 because Netlify had no SPA fallback rule.

To fix both issues, a `netlify.toml` was added at the repository root that:

- Sets the build command to `npm run build` so Vite produces the production bundle.
- Sets the publish directory to `dist`, so Netlify serves the compiled `index.html` (which references the hashed JS/CSS in `/assets/`) instead of the source template.
- Adds a catch-all redirect from `/*` to `/index.html` with status 200, enabling client-side routing for all React Router paths.

After the next deploy, `pairahan.netlify.app` should render the Pairahan Design Consultants site, and direct navigation or refresh on any route should work.

## Summary

This branch delivers six improvements to the highlight system, plus a critical reload bug found and fixed via runtime log analysis:

1. **Right-click context menu for deleting highlights** — replaces the old inline tooltip with a native-feeling context menu that doesn't block right-click on hyperlinks inside highlights.
2. **Compound highlight support** — selections that cross inline elements (`<a>`, `<sup>`, etc.) are wrapped segment-by-segment, stored as a single group, and deleted or overlaid as a unit.
3. **Correct overlap/remainder handling** — when a new highlight colour overlaps an existing one, all non-overlapping portions (prefix, suffix, and middle) are preserved and reapply correctly on reload.
4. **Cross-node reapplication fallback** — on reload, highlights whose stored text spans multiple text nodes (e.g. Wikipedia sentences broken by citation links) now fall back to a document-wide text buffer instead of being silently dropped.
5. **Export / Import** — all highlights can be downloaded as a JSON file and restored on another device or after a browser wipe, with sync quota fallback handled on import.
6. **Clear all highlights** — a quiet "Clear all highlights" action in the popup purges every stored highlight from both sync and local storage, with a confirmation prompt. Non-highlight settings (enabled toggle, blur text, colour choice) are untouched.

---

## Changes

### Right-click delete

The old hover-tooltip delete button was replaced with a context menu triggered by right-clicking any highlight span. The menu dismisses on click-outside, scroll, or Escape. Because it's triggered by `contextmenu` rather than sitting on top of the text, right-clicking a link inside a highlight now correctly passes through to the browser's native menu.

### Compound highlights

When a selection crosses an inline element boundary, the highlight is applied to each text node individually. All the resulting spans share a `data-group` attribute so they behave as one unit — right-clicking any segment deletes the whole group, and overlaying with a new colour replaces the whole group. Storage records a single entry with a `groupId` and `compound: true` flag.

### Overlap and remainder handling

Previously, highlighting over part of an existing highlight could silently erase the non-overlapping portion. Now, when a new selection overlaps an existing highlight:
- The touched entries are removed from storage.
- Any untouched portions (left edge, right edge, or both sides of a middle-overlap) are captured as new remainder entries and written back.
- On reload, remainders are reapplied like any other highlight, so nothing is lost.

### Cross-node reapplication fallback (bug fix)

The reload pipeline had a two-pass design: Pass 1 locates each highlight's text in the DOM, Pass 2 wraps it. Pass 1 uses a single-text-node search, so any highlight whose stored text spans multiple nodes (split by inline tags) was silently skipped — it never reached Pass 2 and was never counted as a failure. The only visible symptom was a mismatch between items stored and items actually applied on reload.

Fix: items that Pass 1 cannot locate, plus items whose Pass 2 wrap fails after earlier wraps split text nodes, are collected and re-attempted using the same document-wide concat buffer that compound highlights already use. No new mechanism — the fallback reuses existing infrastructure.

### Export / Import

The Export button serialises all URL-keyed highlight data to a dated `.json` file that downloads immediately. The Import button reads a file in that format and writes each page's highlights back to storage, respecting the per-item sync quota limit.

### Clear all highlights

A small "Clear all highlights" link sits at the bottom of the Highlighting section. It's intentionally low-profile — muted grey text with a trash icon, turns red on hover. Clicking it shows a confirmation prompt. On confirm, it removes every URL-keyed key from both sync and local storage in parallel; on cancel, nothing changes. A success alert prompts the user to reload open pages, since the visual highlights on the page are not automatically removed (they disappear naturally on next load).

---

## Testing checklist

- [x] Highlight text on a plain paragraph, reload the page — highlight reappears in the same position
- [x] Highlight text that contains a hyperlink — highlight spans the link correctly and reappears after reload
- [x] Highlight a sentence on a Wikipedia page that contains footnote citations (`[1]`, `[2]`) — highlight reappears after reload (this was previously broken)
- [x] Right-click a highlight — a "Delete highlight" context menu appears; selecting it removes the highlight; it is gone after reload
- [x] Right-click any individual segment of a compound highlight (one that spans a link) — the entire highlight group is deleted in one action
- [x] Right-click a hyperlink that sits inside a highlight — the browser's native link context menu appears, not the extension's delete menu
- [x] Highlight "ABCDEF" in yellow, then highlight "CD" in blue — "AB" and "EF" stay yellow after reload; "CD" is blue
- [x] Highlight "ABCDEF" in yellow, then highlight "ABCD" in blue — "EF" stays yellow after reload; "ABCD" is blue
- [x] Delete the blue "ABCD" highlight — "ABCD" reverts to unformatted; "EF" still yellow; no ghost highlights on reload
- [x] Click Export — a `.json` file downloads; opening it shows all highlighted pages and their entries
- [x] Click Import with the exported file — on the relevant pages, highlights restore after reload
- [x] Click "Clear all highlights", then cancel at the confirmation prompt — storage is unchanged, highlights still present
- [x] Click "Clear all highlights" and confirm — all highlights are gone after reloading any previously highlighted page; the enabled toggle, blur text, and colour selection are unaffected; running `chrome.storage.sync.get(null, console.log)` in the extension's service worker console shows no `http`-prefixed keys

### Motivation

- Provide a clear, machine-friendly contract for the Milestone 2 retrieval-only API to allow backend and frontend teams to implement and test retrieval independently of LLM generation.
- Specify deterministic ranking behavior, default and maximum `k` values, and tie-breakers to ensure repeatable, debuggable evidence selection.
- Define strict filtering and scoping rules so only eligible (retrievable + embedded + vector-backed) blocks are returned and to avoid accidental data leakage.

- Added a new "Milestone 2 Retrieval API Contract" section to `docs/rag_pipeline_status.md` that documents the `POST /api/conversations/<conversation_id>/retrieval` endpoint and JSON request/response schemas.
