author: copilot
body:
Aliases are a parallel naming layer over canonical model IDs with no real benefit for agent workflows. They're frozen to specific version strings (silently go stale), encode opinions (`fast-general`, `best-general`) that `find_models_by_criteria` handles better with real data, and contained a priority-inversion bug where system aliases shadowed DB overrides.

## Removed
- `aliasService.ts` — `SYSTEM_ALIASES`, `InMemoryAliasService`, `AliasLookup`
- `types/alias.ts` — `Alias`, `AliasRow`, `AliasScope`
- `list_aliases` MCP tool
- `resolveAlias()` / `listDbAliases()` from `db.ts`
- `aliases` table DDL from `migrate.ts` and seed data from `seed.ts`
- `AliasSchema` from validation schemas

## Simplified
- `ModelRegistry` no longer accepts an `aliasLookup`; `resolve()` is now a straight canonical-ID lookup. `source` union narrows to `'canonical' | 'normalized'`.
- `resolve_model` MCP tool and both `/api/resolve` route handlers strip all alias logic.

Agents should discover models via `search_models` / `find_models_by_criteria` and reference them by canonical ID (e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`).

author: jonmatum
body:
## Summary

Phase 4f. Root app-shell orchestrator that composes all Phase 4 pieces (Sidebar, TopBar, CommandBar, Footer) into a single `<AppShell>` component with slot props and density wiring. Also fixes the CI OOM failure from #34 by splitting the command-bar module.

Refs #5 · Refs #13.

## What's in the box

### `<AppShell>` — root layout orchestrator

| Prop | Type | Default | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|---------|
| `sidebar` | `ReactNode` | — | Content inside `<Sidebar>`. Omit to hide sidebar entirely |
| `defaultSidebarOpen` | `boolean` | `true` | SSR cookie default |
| `sidebarOpen` / `onSidebarOpenChange` | controlled | — | External sidebar control |
| `topBarLeft` / `topBarCenter` / `topBarRight` | `ReactNode` | — | TopBar slot props |
| `topBarSticky` | `boolean` | `true` | Sticky positioning |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` | — | Renders inside `<Footer>`. Omit to hide |
| `commandBarShortcut` | `string \| null` | `'k'` | ⌘K binding; `null` disables |
| `commandBarOpen` / `onCommandBarOpenChange` | controlled | — | External command bar control |
| `density` | `'compact' \| 'comfortable' \| 'spacious'` | `'comfortable'` | Sets `data-density` on root for CSS scoping |

Composition tree:
```
CommandBarProvider
  SidebarProvider [data-slot="app-shell"] [data-density]
    Sidebar (optional)
    SidebarInset (<main>)
      TopBar
      CommandBar (portal)
      div[data-slot="app-shell-body"]
        {children}
      Footer (optional)
```

### Command-bar context split (fixes #34 CI)

Extracted `command-bar-context.tsx` (lightweight: React context, hooks, provider — only depends on React) from `command-bar.tsx` (heavy UI: cmdk, Radix Dialog, lucide icons). The test file now imports from the context module, eliminating the OOM that was killing CI.

- `command-bar.tsx` re-exports everything from `command-bar-context.tsx` so the public API is unchanged
- No barrel export changes needed — consumers still import from `@jonmatum/next-shell/layout`

## What is NOT in this PR

- Density CSS custom properties (deferred to Phase 8 utilities)
- `CommandBarTrigger` unit tests (removed to avoid heavy deps; covered by Storybook/Playwright in Phase 9)
- Server-side rendering of AppShell (it's client-only by design)

## Verification

```
pnpm format     ✅
pnpm lint       ✅ (0 warnings)
pnpm typecheck  ✅
pnpm test       ✅ 15 files, 385 tests passed (no OOM)
pnpm build      ✅
```

## Checklist

- [x] No raw color literals
- [x] `data-slot="app-shell"` + `data-slot="app-shell-body"` on layout elements
- [x] `data-density` attribute for downstream CSS scoping
- [x] Controlled + uncontrolled modes for both sidebar and command bar
- [x] Optional sidebar (omit prop to hide)
- [x] Optional footer (omit prop to hide)
- [x] Command-bar context split fixes CI OOM
- [x] 11 new AppShell tests + 5 command-bar context tests

body:
#### 4216f6e6461a64bfde017ae0bcf193f7af1bbef0 
Removing/outdent a line from ordered list causes the following list to start with an incorrect number
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=312522
rdar://173537449

Reviewed by Aditya Keerthi.

In unlistifyParagraph, there isn't a procedure to set the
starting list number after splitting. So, when it calls
splitElement() to split the list, this calls
Element::cloneElementWithoutChildren which clones all attributes,
including the start attribute.

For example, if the original list started with 11 and the list
is split in the middle, both lists now start with 11. The
expectation is when splitting the list, the second list starts
from 1.

Thus, make a function that splits the list and sets the second starting
list number to be 1 if a start attribute was originally provided. Otherwise,
don't do anything. Now, outdenting, removing list formatting, and entering to
create new lines should all have the following list start with 1.

Additionally, add layout tests for the cases to confirm the correct
starting list numbers. For outdenting and remove list formatting, both
go down the same code path so there is only one test.

This pull request updates the GitHub Actions workflow configuration in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to use newer versions of several actions and improves the setup for Python and .NET environments. The main focus is on keeping dependencies up-to-date and making the CI setup more robust and efficient.

**GitHub Actions version upgrades:**

* Updated `actions/checkout` from v4 to v6 in both job sections to use the latest version. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b803fcb7f17ed9235f1e5cb1fcd2f5d3b2838429d4368ae4c57ce4436577f03fL18-R21) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b803fcb7f17ed9235f1e5cb1fcd2f5d3b2838429d4368ae4c57ce4436577f03fL61-R86)

author: okuyam2y
body: ## Summary When models fail to escape double quotes inside JSON string values, the tool call is rejected entirely. This adds a `repairToolCallJson` fallback that attempts to recover the tool call by: 1. Extracting the tool name via `extractTopLevelStringProperty` (depth-aware) 2. Locating the `arguments` object via `findTopLevelPropertyValueStart` (top-level aware) 3. Splitting by key positions with optional schema-aware filtering (`knownArgKeys` from tool definitions) 4. Repairing each string value by escaping unescaped quotes The repair is best-effort — returns `null` when repair is not possible, falling through to the existing `onError` path. Also threads the `tools` parameter through `processToolCallJson` / `processMatchedToolCall` / `ParseContext` to enable schema-aware key filtering. **Known limitations:** - `arguments` must be the last top-level property (backwards `}}` scan) - Unknown extra keys are dropped when schema filtering is active - Non-string values that fail `JSON.parse` cause the repair to bail out (no type coercion) Closes #298 ## Test plan - 15 new test cases (13 non-streaming, 2 streaming) - Unescaped quotes in single and multiple arguments - Schema-aware key filtering (false-positive `,"fake":` patterns) - Valid JSON passthrough (no regression) - Completely broken JSON falls through to `onError` - Numeric, boolean, null values alongside broken strings - Nested objects and arrays without false key splits - Nested `"name"` inside arguments not confused with tool name - Non-string parse failure returns `null` (type coercion prevention) - Arguments-not-last-property graceful failure - 100KB size guard - Streaming repair on complete tool calls --- ## Summary by cubic Adds best‑effort repair for malformed tool call JSON when models don’t escape quotes in string arguments, so valid tool calls aren’t dropped. Enforces strict schema semantics during repair in `hermes-protocol` across parse and streaming; strict‑JSON only, with hardened edge cases, bounded recursion to prevent stack overflows, and safe full‑text fallback when repair isn’t possible. - **Bug Fixes** - Schema: honor wrapped schemas; enforce nested shapes and `patternProperties`; reject unknown/invalid keys under strict policy; distinguish `oneOf` branches; validate key–value shape matches; fail‑closed on unsafe deny classes; bound recursive validation (max depth 256) to avoid stack overflow; reject null arguments when disallowed and preserve `null` when allowed. - Key detection: depth‑ and top‑level aware detection of "name"/"arguments"; keep all top‑level key boundaries; score duplicate keys; require own top‑level fields. - Filtering: apply schema checks only at assignment; drop schema‑unknown keys; bail if all parsed keys are unknown; compile safe pattern regexes; deny unsafe/backreference patterns. - Repair: escape unescaped quotes in string values; catch‑all around repair to return `null` on unexpected errors; bail on non‑string parse failures, ambiguous `,"unknown":` inside broken strings, or arguments body >100KB. - Streaming: emit progress safely (including before delayed closing tags); preserve full original text on bailout; block unsafe progress paths. Written for commit f030717350bb6469a150e0748965e9dac2c76953. Summary will update on new commits.

## Summary

GH#19423 (PR #19425) ratcheted `BASH32_COMPAT_THRESHOLD` from 78 to 74, claiming 72 actual violations. CI against the merged PR reported **76 violations** vs the new threshold 74 — main had drifted from 72 to 76 between issue filing and PR merge.

grep BASH32_COMPAT_THRESHOLD .agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf

body:
## Summary

Implements persistent report artifacts and the automated daily paper-trading validation report job.

---

## Changes

### Migration 000029 — `report_artifacts` table
- New table with composite unique key `(strategy_id, report_type, time_bucket)`
- Descending index on `(strategy_id, report_type, completed_at)` for fast latest-report lookups
- Status enum: `pending` | `completed` | `error`

### `ReportArtifactRepo` (`internal/repository/postgres/report_artifact.go`)
- `Upsert` — insert or update-on-conflict; idempotent per (strategy, type, bucket)
- `GetLatest` — returns most recent `status=completed` artifact for a strategy+type
- `List` — paginated list with `ReportArtifactFilter` (strategy_id, report_type, status)

### `paper_validation_report` automation job (`internal/automation/jobs_reports.go`)
- Scheduled daily at 17:00 ET Mon–Fri (after market close), weekdays only
- Iterates all active paper strategies; failures are isolated (one bad strategy won't block others)
- Loads latest backtest run → deserialises `backtest.Metrics` → calls `papervalidation.GenerateReport`
- Persists `ReportArtifact` with `status=completed`; on error writes `status=error` artifact
- 0–120s jitter between strategies to spread DB/CPU load
- Gracefully skips registration when `ReportArtifactRepo` is nil (e.g. smoke env)

### REST endpoints (`internal/api/report_handlers.go`)
- `GET /api/v1/strategies/{id}/reports/latest` — latest completed report; includes `stale_seconds`
- `GET /api/v1/strategies/{id}/reports` — paginated history; supports `?report_type=` and `?status=` filters
- Returns `501 Not Implemented` when repo not wired (graceful degradation)

### Wiring
- `OrchestratorDeps` gains `ReportArtifactRepo`, `BacktestConfigRepo`, `BacktestRunRepo`
- `api.Deps` / `api.Server` gain `ReportArtifacts *pgrepo.ReportArtifactRepo`
- `runtime.go` constructs and distributes the repo to both orchestrator and API server

### Pre-existing fix
- Removed duplicate `validateFallbackProvider` declaration in `internal/config/validate.go` (caused build failure before this PR)

---

## Schema bump

`RequiredSchemaVersion`: **28 → 29**

Run `task migrate` before deploying.

---

## Tests
- `internal/repository/postgres/report_artifact_test.go` — struct JSON round-trip, filter defaults
- `internal/automation/jobs_reports_test.go` — nil repo guard, no paper strategies, no backtest configs, generation flow
- `internal/api/report_handlers_test.go` — 501 when unconfigured, 400 on invalid UUID, `stale_seconds` serialization

🧨 **The Trigger:** Calling `StringBuilder.delete(start, end)` with `start > end`, `start < 0`, or `start` greater than the string's character length bypassed bounds checking. This caused the underlying Rust `String::drain()` or `buf.char_indices().nth()` logic to panic, crashing the VM with a slice bounds error instead of failing gracefully.

📉 **The Stack Trace:**
```
thread 'main' panicked at:
slice index starts at X but ends at Y
```

🧪 **Reproduction:**
Write a mock Java test invoking `new StringBuilder("hello").delete(3, 2);` which triggers the panic.

😈 **Comment:**
You assumed Java callers would never pass negative or inverted bounds to `StringBuilder.delete`. You were wrong. Fixed by validating bounds and gracefully throwing `VmError::ArrayIndexOutOfBounds` instead. Added `test_sb_delete_out_of_bounds` unit test.

author: shukwong
body:
Critical fixes:
- Wire up BacalhauTaskMonitor via createTaskMonitor() override; it was
  dead code before — Nextflow instantiated the generic HPC-tuned monitor.
- Stop holding queueStatusLock across the CLI subprocess: on cache miss,
  only one thread fetches while concurrent callers return the last known
  snapshot, so polling is no longer serialized behind a 60s CLI call.
- Add failure back-off to the queue-status cache so a broken CLI is not
  re-invoked on every poll.
- Track the result-retrieval Thread so kill() can interrupt it; the
  thread is now a named daemon rather than an untracked Thread.start.
- Guard the RUNNING status transition so the state write only fires on
  actual transitions, not every poll.
- Fix extractJobId regex to accept the real Bacalhau 'job-<UUID>' prefix
  (and 'j-<UUID>' as a fallback).
- Avoid NPE on accelerator.request when no GPU is requested.
- formatTimeout now returns 0 on unparseable values so the timeout block
  is omitted rather than falling back to the submit timeout.
- validateHostPath matches '..' path segments, not a substring, so
  legitimate paths like /data/foo..bar are no longer rejected.
- Move the script mount from /tmp to /nextflow-scripts so it does not
  overlay the container's own tmpfs.
- Make bacalhauJobId volatile for safe cross-thread reads.

Pre-existing compile errors against the declared Nextflow 23.10.1 API:
- TaskStatus has no ERROR value; failures now go through markFailed()
  which sets task.error + non-zero exitStatus + status=COMPLETED.
- Qualify QueueStatus import in BacalhauTaskHandler.
- getEnvironment() lives on TaskRun, not TaskConfig; ext is a map entry
  accessed via task.config.get('ext').
- TaskPollingMonitor has no builder(); use the Map-arg super constructor.
- BacalhauPlugin: replace @Slf4j (collides with Plugin.log) with an
  explicit SLF4J logger.

Tests:
- Replace mocks of final methods (AcceleratorResource.getRequest,
  MemoryUnit.toBytes) with real instances.
- S3 Path uses a toString-stubbed Mock since Path.of('s3://…') makes a
  local path on Linux.
- Move getEnvironment from TaskConfig mock to TaskRun mock.
- Error path uses Spock interactions on task.setError/setExitStatus
  because the TaskRun mock doesn't retain field writes.
- Add byte-buddy + objenesis so Spock can mock classes at runtime.

author: herbenderbler
body:
## Description

**Related to** https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/21140 — do **not** use `Fixes #21140` until there is evidence of a clear improvement; keep the issue open for now.

### Background

[#21140](https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/21140) reports intermittent stalls on GitHub Actions **macOS**: `runtests.pl` shows one runner still busy (often with **FTP-related** tests), sometimes until the job step timeout. Maintainer feedback included a repro stuck on **test 575** with **`ST_RUN`** ([comment](https://github.com/curl/curl/pull/21350#issuecomment-4426718680)): that state means the **libtest client** was still running, not necessarily the in-tree FTP server.

### What this PR does

**Scope:** `tests/ftpserver.pl` and `tests/libtest/lib575.c`.

1. **FTP test server:** `sysread_or_die` uses a bounded `select()` (currently **65s** per wait; see comment in file vs **TEST_HANG_TIMEOUT**) before `sysread` on sockfilt. This extends the same pattern to **data** pipe reads in **`disc_handshake`** and **`STOR_ftp`** so a stuck sockfilt cannot block those paths indefinitely.

2. **Test 575:** Set **`CURLOPT_TIMEOUT_MS`** to **`TEST_HANG_TIMEOUT`** (same idea as **lib574**) so each **`curl_easy_perform`** cannot hang until an external CI timeout. **`start_test_timing()`** runs **only before the multi phase** so the usual **60s** wall-clock guard does not false-positive when two sequential performs legitimately exceed **60s** wall time on slow CI.

## Implementation details

- `tests/ftpserver.pl`: `sysread_or_die` on `DREAD` in `disc_handshake` and `STOR_ftp`; control path already uses `sysread_or_die` with the same select ceiling.
- `tests/libtest/lib575.c`: `CURLOPT_TIMEOUT_MS`; hang timer reset before multi; `abort_on_test_timeout()` remains in the multi loop only.

body:
## Summary

Fixes unbounded nginx access log growth (298Mi/day/pod observed in production) by wiring the already-present s6-log producer-consumer pipeline correctly, retires the `logger` workaround service, and ships chart hygiene defaults so the temporary `apps` namespace LimitRange override in iac can be removed.

- **Image:** nginx + php-fpm now write to stdout/stderr → feeds the existing s6-log pipeline that tees to rotated file + stdout. `logger` tail-loop service removed. `nginx-log-prepare` / `php-fpm-log-prepare` oneshots now template the `run` scripts from `SAIL_LOG_MODE|MAX_ARCHIVES|ROTATE_SIZE` env vars.
- **Chart:** new `<name>-defaults` Secret (chart-owned) prepended to `envFrom` so `LOG_CHANNEL=stderr` (plus conditional `CACHE_DRIVER`/`SESSION_DRIVER=redis` when `redis.secret` is set) apply by default but consumers can override via their `<name>-environment` secret (envFrom later-entry-wins). New `sail.resources` helper with tier→global→hardcoded fallback (CPU 100m/1000m, Memory 256Mi/1Gi).
- **Values surface:** new `sail.logging.{mode,maxArchives,maxFileSize}` + `sail.app.{logChannel,cacheDriver,sessionDriver}` blocks, documented in `values.stub`.

## Behavior changes consumers should know

- **`kubectl logs` output format changes shape.** Previously all `*.log` files were tailed with `[filename]` prefix by the retired `logger` service. Now stdout shows nginx + php-fpm + Laravel app logs with `[nginx]` / `[php-fpm]` prefixes, in write order.
- **`/var/log/nginx/nginx.access.log` and `nginx.error.log` no longer exist.** Rotated archives now live at `/var/log/nginx/current` + `@<tai64n>.s.gz`. Consumers with log-forwarder configs pointed at the old paths must update.
- **Laravel `storage/logs/laravel.log` no longer written by default.** `LOG_CHANNEL` defaults to `stderr`. Consumers relying on the on-disk file set `sail.app.logChannel: stack` / `daily`.
- **Default container resources added.** Consumers on capacity-constrained clusters may see scheduling pressure on first redeploy; set `resources` overrides in their values to mitigate.

## Related

- Spec 1 (disk pressure mitigation in nimbus): `ReyemTech/nimbus` ships per-pod ephemeral-storage LimitRanges, plus an `apps` namespace override (1Gi/5Gi) that was introduced pending this PR
- Follow-up (not part of this PR): once this ships and runs 24h without eviction events, delete the `namespacePolicies.apps` override block from `iac/src/index.ts` and `pulumi up`

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: `vendor/bin/phpunit` (36 tests pass locally — 19 Feature + 17 Integration)
- [ ] CI: `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse src --memory-limit=512M` (clean locally)
- [ ] Manual: `helm template` against a booklet/gta-events/reyemtech-shaped values file produces valid YAML (verified locally with `kubectl apply --dry-run=client`)
- [ ] Manual: build the image from this branch, boot it, `docker logs` shows nginx + php-fpm output with `[nginx]`/`[php-fpm]` prefixes, `/var/log/nginx/current` grows under load
- [ ] Manual: once one consumer deploys this image, confirm `kubectl exec -n apps <pod> -c web -- ls -la /var/log/nginx/` shows `current` (growing) and no `nginx.access.log`
- [ ] Manual: 24h after all consumers roll, `kubectl top nodes` and kubelet stats show per-pod ephemeral usage stable under 100Mi (down from ~340Mi baseline)

body:
Closes #136

## What

Two E2E failures detected after PR #134:

1. **Re-invite toast not shown** — The `InviteForm` blocked re-inviting when a pending invite already existed, showing "An invite has already been sent to this email." instead of "Invite sent." This happened because the previous revoke's database delete could fail silently (Supabase RLS-blocked deletes return success with 0 rows affected), leaving a stale invite record.

2. **Search empty state missing** — The "No pages match your search" message depended on `workspaceResolved`, which could create a timing gap where neither the skeleton nor the empty state rendered. When the workspace resolution was slow, the search callback returned early (no `workspaceId`), set `loading = false`, but `workspaceResolved` was still `false` — showing skeletons indefinitely until a second search cycle completed.

## How

1. **InviteForm**: Changed the duplicate-invite check from blocking with an error to deleting the existing invite before creating a new one. This makes re-inviting idempotent — it works whether the previous invite was properly revoked or not.

2. **PageSearch**: Added a `searched` flag that only becomes `true` after a real API call completes (not after an early return due to missing `workspaceId`). The empty state condition now uses `searched` instead of `workspaceResolved`, ensuring the empty state only appears after the search API has actually responded with zero results.

## Testing

- All 125 unit tests pass (`pnpm test`)
- All 42 E2E tests pass (`pnpm test:e2e`), including the two previously failing tests:
  - `e2e/members.spec.ts:139` — "owner can re-invite and invited user can accept" ✅
  - `e2e/search.spec.ts:159` — "search with no matches shows empty state" ✅
- Existing `page-search.test.tsx` unit tests (3 tests) continue to pass with the `searched` flag change
- Lint and typecheck clean

## Problem

The root `main.py` was a plain script containing only a `main()` function that printed a string. Uvicorn's deploy command (`uvicorn main:app`) expects an `app` attribute in that module, causing an "Attribute 'app' not found in module 'main'" error on every deploy.

Rewrote `main.py` to re-export the `app` instance from `backend/main.py`, where the full FastAPI application (routes, middleware, lifespan, exception handlers) is already defined. This gives uvicorn exactly the `main:app` target it needs without duplicating any application logic.

- Add a narrowly scoped legal enrichment so employment-law financial/entitlement questions (compensation promised, unpaid amounts, bonus entitlement, vacation pay, reimbursements, severance, and what financial records support a claim) are recognized and answered using responsive financial evidence instead of unrelated clause text.
- Preserve the existing retrieval pipeline and general RAG behavior while enforcing stricter answerability for financial questions and failing safely when financial evidence is missing or ambiguous.

body:
## Summary

Voice mode can now proactively pull illustrative photos from Unsplash when the user asks to see pictures of something, or when the AI judges that a few photos would make a spoken explanation clearer. Photos render inline in the chat via the same ImageGrid used by text mode.

Also bumps the Vite dev port from 2005 → 2006 (config update only; no behavior impact).

## What changed

**Backend (mirrored in Vercel `api/*` + Express `server/`)**
- `api/search-images.ts` (new) + `POST /api/search-images` route in `server/src/routes/chat.ts` — thin wrapper around the existing Unsplash helper
- `api/realtime/token.ts` + `server/src/routes/chat.ts` — register `search_images` as a second Realtime tool next to `browse_url`; update session instructions so the AI speaks a one-sentence intro like "Let me pull up some photos of X" before calling

**Frontend**
- `src/lib/realtime.ts` — handle the `search_images` function call in `handleFunctionCall`, deliver results via a new `onImages` callback, and feed a concise tool-output back to the AI so it keeps speaking naturally instead of re-listing URLs
- `src/components/VoiceMode.tsx`, `src/components/ChatPanel.tsx`, `src/App.tsx` — thread `onImages` through; `handleVoiceImages` appends an assistant message with `imageResults` populated, so the existing ChatMessage renderer picks them up unchanged

**Config**
- `vite.config.ts` + `.claude/launch.json` — dev server port 2005 → 2006 (strictPort)

## Why

Voice mode was text-only; adding image search means an AI explanation about "golden retrievers" or "cherry blossoms" can include real photos without the user having to drop out of voice mode and type. Reusing the existing Unsplash path from text mode keeps behavior consistent across modes.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Deployment requires `UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY` in Vercel env vars** (Production + Preview + Development). Without it, the tool registers but returns an empty list and the AI apologizes gracefully.
- The Realtime tool description nudges the AI to be proactive; if it feels over-eager in practice, tighten the wording in `api/realtime/token.ts` / `server/src/routes/chat.ts`.
- Port bump is a pure config change — nothing downstream references 2005.

body:
## Summary

Adds a new `pitstop-truth` receipt for `TalonT-Org/AutoSkillit#992`, capturing a reusable execution-shape failure:

> secondary rate limits triggered by unbatched mutation loops and bursty write patterns under a shared API budget

This is not primarily a retry bug. It is a workflow-design failure where individually reasonable GitHub operations compose into avoidable throttling.

---

## Why this matters

The issue explicitly distinguishes between:

- retry resilience improvements already made in `#892`
- and the deeper root cause that remained: excessive API call volume created by execution shape

That makes this a strong receipt because it shows:

- resilience patches can improve survival behavior without fixing root cause
- shared external budgets must be treated as a design constraint
- batching and serialization are correctness concerns, not just optimizations

---

## Hazard classes

- `rate_limit_429`
- `retry_budget_exhausted`

---

## Key signals captured

- secondary rate limits hit during PR review workflows
- per-comment POST fallback consumes 5 points per mutation
- thread replies and resolutions executed individually
- GitHub requires 1s spacing between mutating requests
- retry resilience previously improved but did not resolve the issue
- batch endpoints reduce many writes to a single request

---

## Reusable lesson

This receipt captures a broader pattern:

> systems can respect retry/backoff and still fail if they generate unnecessary mutation density under shared budgets

The important fix class is not just “wait longer after rate limits.”

It is:

- batch writes
- serialize mutations
- prefetch shared reads
- reduce avoidable pressure before limits are hit

---

author: tanaymit
body:
# What Non-Safety Signals Are Actually Worth Your Time

## What I Found

I analyzed 231 non-safety use cases extracted from customer calls to answer: **which ones are real opportunities, and which are extraction noise?**

### Key Finding: 69.3% of rows are questionable

Non-safety rows hit trust flags for:
- Generic/admin language (33.8%)
- Weak label-evidence match (65.4%)
- Voxel-only speaker evidence (32.0%)
- Safety concept overlap (13.4%)

After filtering, the real signal concentrates in **3 themes:**

| Theme | Calls | Evidence Quality |
|-------|-------|------------------|
| Reporting & Analytics | 11 | 50% customer-sourced |
| Workflow & Accountability | 10 | 45% customer-sourced |
| Asset & Loss Prevention | 4 | 50% customer-sourced |

## The Problem

The extraction pipeline is useful but overconfident. Labels often don't match their evidence (median Jaccard overlap: 5.3%). It's like a strong intern who needs verification before you trust the output.

## The Solution

Simple: flag low-trust rows, review those + a small random sample weekly. Takes ~30 min/week, eliminates 95% of noise.

## What's Included

- **`voxel_tanaymittal.ipynb`** – Full reproducible analysis with all charts and methodology
- **`tanay_mittal_voxel.pptx`** – 5-slide deck with key findings
- **`SUBMISSION.md`** – Full approach, assumptions, and limitations
- **`clean_non_safety_theme_rank.csv`** – Ranked themes after cleaning
- **`nonsafety_trust_audit_rows.csv`** – Complete audit data with trust flags
- **`manual_fidelity_sample.csv`** – 60-row stratified sample ready for manual review

## TL;DR

The extraction works, but use it as a lead list, not as gospel. Trust-gate it, and you'll focus on real opportunities instead of chasing noise.

author: copilot
body:
Codifies the memory policy layer that was missing between Phase 1.9 (context budgeting) and Phase 2 (RAG): the *what* and *why* of storing, not just the *how*.

## New phase: 1.95 — Memory Strategy & Intelligence

### Short-Term Memory Policy (`1.95.1`)
- Recency window tied to Phase 1.9 token budget
- Relevance pre-filter before appending turns (skips filler/small talk)
- Entity/state replacement instead of appending duplicates
- Overflow compression via summarisation rather than blind truncation

### Long-Term Memory Policy (`1.95.2`)
- Explicit vs. implicit signal distinction; implicit facts require ≥3 observations before storage
- Novelty check — skip if the candidate is a restatement of existing memory
- Stability heuristic with a `transient: true` flag for short-lived facts
- Confidence threshold (default `0.8`) gating soul/RAG writes
- Decay via `last_reinforced` timestamp; stale entries flagged after 30 days
- Category whitelist: `user_preferences`, `biographical_facts`, `domain_expertise_level`, `project_context`

### Memory Decision Flow (`1.95.3`)
`should_store()` in `src/memory/policy.py` runs a four-gate chain — repeat? incidental? transient? low-confidence? — and returns a `(bool, reason)` tuple consumed by both the soul-update path and the future RAG write path.

### Two-Pass Extraction Architecture (`1.95.4`)
Separates conversation handling from memory extraction: a lightweight `MemoryExtractor` daemon thread runs an isolated `MEMORY_EXTRACT_PROMPT` (in `src/llm/prompts.py`) after each turn, calls `should_store()`, and logs every decision to `data/logs/memory.log` — the stub wired in Phase 1.8.5.

author: smolkaj
body:
## Summary

Smallest possible first lever from `designs/parallel_packet_scaling.md`
candidate (1). Replaces the expensive `value < BigInteger.TWO.pow(width)`
bounds check in `BitVector.<init>` with `value.bitLength() <= width`,
and `value >= BigInteger.ZERO` with `value.signum() >= 0`.

Both are mathematically equivalent for the non-negative values
`BitVector` holds. Both avoid allocation / nested comparison work
that the originals performed on every construction.

## Why this is the first thing to ship

Phase 2.5 profile had `BitVector.<init>` at **13.5% of parallel CPU**
— the single biggest hot spot, driving most of the `BigInteger`
category that dominates the sequential/parallel diff. The full Long
fast path (eliminating BigInteger storage entirely for widths ≤ 63)
is multi-day work. This commit captures a big chunk of the savings
in a one-line change with zero semantic risk.

## Measured (AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D, SAI middleblock, 5-run medians)

| | Sequential | Parallel | Speedup | Efficiency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline (main) | 209 pps | 1,500 pps | 7.18× | **44.9%** |
| This commit | **231 pps** | **1,795 pps** | 7.77× | **48.6%** |
| Δ | **+10.5%** | **+19.7%** | | **+3.7 pp** |

Parallel speedup (+19.7%) is ~2× sequential speedup (+10.5%), so this
is an efficiency lever, not just an absolute-throughput win.

## Correctness

`bitLength()` returns the minimum number of bits needed to represent
the magnitude. For non-negative values, `value < 2^width ⇔
bitLength ≤ width`. Proof sketch:

- `value = 0`: bitLength = 0; satisfies `bitLength ≤ width` for any
  `width ≥ 0`. Also handles the `width == 0` edge case uniformly
  (requires bitLength = 0, i.e. value = 0).
- `value = 2^width − 1`: bitLength = width; at the boundary, accepted
  by both forms.
- `value = 2^width`: bitLength = width + 1; rejected by both forms.

`signum() >= 0` is trivially equivalent to `value >= BigInteger.ZERO`
(signum returns -1/0/+1).

## Cross-check against an oracle

Ran a separate variant that skipped validation entirely for widths
≤ 63: +12.8% parallel / +6.2% sequential — *less* than this commit.
The oracle's branch in `init` hurt JIT inlining; the straight-line
bitLength-based init in this commit is tighter than skipping
validation via a conditional. Oracle code not included in this PR.

## Follow-up

Scaling-doc candidate (1) predicted ~20-25% absolute / ~12%
efficiency ceiling for the *full* Long fast path (replacing
BigInteger storage). This commit delivers ~20% absolute / 4 pp
efficiency — roughly the "validation-only" slice of that ceiling.
Full Long fast path remains available to pursue; file a separate
issue if we want to go further.

## Test plan

- [x] `bazel test //... --test_tag_filters=-heavy` — all 64 pass
- [x] `./tools/format.sh` clean
- [x] `./tools/lint.sh` clean
- [x] Benchmark 5 runs each of sequential and parallel, both
      baseline and this commit
- [ ] CI green

author: lbenedetto
body: Perfectly replicate the behaviour from IntelliJ, with one added improvement: When importing with `@`, your current file is used to boost the score of any files which are nearby Previously, every single keystroke uses rg to list all files in the project and then applies fuzzy matching. This happens in no more than 50ms (usually <20ms) in my project with 361 files, but it seems like an approach which does not scale well. ripgrep is the biggest bottleneck here so I applied caching by creating a sessionId when you open a search dialogue so that subsequent requests with that key reused the previously fetched list of files and just applies filtering. A new sessionId (new every time you open the dialogue) overwrites the cache so it can't get out sync. Now opening the dialogue pays the penalty of loading a list of files (50ms) and subsequent keystrokes just operate on the list in memory (10ms). I think it's safe to assume that files will not be created while you are typing in a search dialogue (and if they are that it's ok if they don't show up until you close and reopen the dialogue). The remaining latency comes from the IPC call as the fuzzy match algorithm takes less than 1ms. [#299](https://github.com/VoidenHQ/voiden/issues/299)

author: suniagajose
body:
## Problem

When an XML file in the inspected module contains no tag (e.g. an empty `.xml` file), `ChecksOdooModuleXML._get_first_tag` returns the Python `str` `''`. The success branch of the same method returns bytes from `b' '.join(buffer)`, and downstream code in `check_xml_header` consumes the result as bytes:

```python
if not first_tag.startswith(b"<?xml "):
```

When `first_tag` is `str`, `startswith(bytes)` raises:

```
TypeError: startswith first arg must be str or a tuple of str, not bytes
```

This crashes the entire hook for the repository as soon as one empty/tag-less XML file exists anywhere in the inspected modules — even if `xml-header-missing` is disabled, because the mismatch happens before the enablement check.

## Reproduction

```python
import io
from oca_pre_commit_hooks.checks_odoo_module_xml import ChecksOdooModuleXML

inst = ChecksOdooModuleXML.__new__(ChecksOdooModuleXML)
result = inst._get_first_tag(io.BytesIO(b''))
# Before fix: ('', 0) — str
# After fix:  (b'', 0) — bytes
```

The existing `test_repo/broken_module/xml_empty.xml` fixture is a 0-byte file and reproduces the issue on real hook runs.

## Fix

Return `b""` instead of `""` in the no-tag path so both branches of `_get_first_tag` are type-consistent (always bytes), and downstream `startswith(b"<?xml ")` / `decode("UTF-8")` calls keep working.

One-line change in `src/oca_pre_commit_hooks/checks_odoo_module_xml.py`.

## Notes

Found while running v0.2.20 against an Odoo 19 addon that contains an empty XML file. The local test suite does not run on Python 3.14 (distutils removed) so verification was done via targeted reproduction; CI will validate against the supported matrix.

author: zachdunn
body:
Closes #269

## Problem

`/v1/stats` returned only `{ orgs, sources, releases, products }`. The CLI's `StatsSummary` response shape was composed from three endpoints (`/v1/stats`, `/v1/fetch-log`, `/v1/sources`), and 7 fields ended up zeroed/empty — breaking the Source Health section in \`releases stats\`.

Hollow fields observed:
- \`releasesInPeriod\`
- \`upToDate\`, \`stale\`, \`neverFetched\`
- \`recentReleases\` (per source)
- \`sourceName\`, \`sourceSlug\` (on recent-activity rows)

## Fix

\`workers/api/src/routes/stats.ts\` — rewrite the route to compute all fields in one response:

- \`?days=N\` query param (default 30) for period windowing
- Filtered counts for \`releasesInPeriod\`
- \`upToDate\` = sources with \`lastFetchedAt >= cutoff\`, \`neverFetched\` = null \`lastFetchedAt\`, \`stale\` = remainder
- Per-source \`totalReleases\` + \`recentReleases\` via GROUP BY join (releases → sources → organizations)
- \`recentActivity\` via fetchLog → sources → organizations, so \`sourceName\` / \`sourceSlug\` / \`orgName\` are populated

Legacy flat fields (\`orgs\`, \`sources\`, \`releases\`, \`products\`) are preserved at the top level for the web homepage banner.

\`src/api/client.ts\` — \`getStatsSummary()\` collapsed to a single \`GET /v1/stats?days=N\` call (was 3 endpoints). Dropped unused \`daysAgoIso\` import.

## Verified

- \`npx tsc --noEmit\` passes

## Not verified

- Didn't hit staging to confirm shape match end-to-end. Worth a smoke test before merge.

author: copilot
body:
Stateless JWTs can't be revoked server-side, and long-lived tokens are a liability. This adds opt-in server-side session tracking with refresh token rotation — both features are strictly additive; existing code without a `SessionStore` is unaffected.

## `auth` package

- **`Session` / `SessionStore`** — new type and 7-method interface for session CRUD; only the SHA-256 hash of the refresh token is persisted
- **`CreateTokenWithSession(ctx, userID, sessionID)`** — embeds session ID as the JWT `jti` claim
- **`ParseTokenClaims(tokenString)`** — validates signature, ignores expiry (used by logout to parse potentially expired access tokens)
- **`Config.Sessions SessionStore`** — when set, `Middleware` and `AdminMiddleware` validate `jti` against the store on every request; API key auth bypasses the check

## `handler` package

- **`AuthHandler`** gains `Sessions`, `RefreshTokenTTL`, `RefreshCookieName` fields
  - `Login`/`Signup` create a session and return `refresh_token` in the response
  - `Logout` revokes the session by extracting `jti` from the (possibly expired) access token
  - New `RefreshToken` handler: validates the refresh token hash, atomically deletes the old session, issues a new session + rotated token pair
- **`SessionHandler`** (new) — `List` (200), `Revoke` (204), `RevokeAll` (204)

## Usage

```go
jwtMgr, _ := auth.NewJWTManager(secret, 15*time.Minute, "myapp") // short-lived access tokens

authHandler := &handler.AuthHandler{
    Users:             userStore,
    JWT:               jwtMgr,
    Sessions:          sessionStore,         // enables everything
    RefreshTokenTTL:   7 * 24 * time.Hour,
    RefreshCookieName: "refresh",            // optional HttpOnly cookie
    CookieName:        "session",
    SecureCookies:     true,
}

sessionHandler := &handler.SessionHandler{
    Sessions:     sessionStore,
    URLParamFunc: chi.URLParam,
}

// Middleware validates jti on every request
cfg := auth.Config{CookieName: "session", Sessions: sessionStore}
r.Use(auth.Middleware(jwtMgr, cfg, apiKeyStore))

r.Post("/auth/refresh",    authHandler.RefreshToken)
r.Get("/sessions",         sessionHandler.List)
r.Delete("/sessions/{id}", sessionHandler.Revoke)
r.Delete("/sessions",      sessionHandler.RevokeAll)
```
